konsumtionsbaserade_utslapp_sverige.name: Consumption-based greenhouse gas emissions per person
konsumtionsbaserade_utslapp_sverige.note: Down about 36% per capita 2008–2023; about 60% comes from household consumption. Considerably higher than the territorial figure of about 4.5 t per inhabitant.
konsumtionsbaserade_utslapp_sverige.unit: t CO2e per person per year

forsorjningsformaga_spannmal_sverige.name: Sweden's self-sufficiency, cereals
forsorjningsformaga_spannmal_sverige.note: The 2023/24 season (weak harvest). Sweden is a net exporter of cereals. The Swedish Board of Agriculture does not report an overall self-sufficiency rate for all food.

forsorjningsformaga_mejeri_sverige.name: Sweden's self-sufficiency, dairy products
forsorjningsformaga_mejeri_sverige.note: Down from 112% in 1995. Cheese only 39%. Eggs 95% (2023, salmonella outbreak).

forsorjningsformaga_tomat_sverige.name: Sweden's self-sufficiency, fresh tomatoes
forsorjningsformaga_tomat_sverige.note: An example of import dependence for fruit and vegetables: apples 29%, cucumbers 48%, strawberries 69%, onions 78%, carrots 97%.

ensamhet_ofta_alltid_sverige.name: Often or always troubled by loneliness
ensamhet_ofta_alltid_sverige.note: National Public Health Survey 2024. A further 13% are sometimes troubled by it.

unga_skarmtid_over_3h.name: 13–16-year-olds with more than 3 hours of leisure screen time per day
unga_skarmtid_over_3h.note: Computer, mobile phone and tablet on a typical day; 93% among 17–18-year-olds. The Public Health Agency of Sweden recommends no more than 2–3 hours for 13–18-year-olds.

internet_dagligen.name: Use the internet daily
internet_dagligen.note: Population aged 16+. 97% use the internet; almost everyone who does not is a pensioner. 4 in 10 Swedes (aged 8+) use AI tools.

hemberedskap_en_vecka.name: Households prepared at home for at least one week
hemberedskap_en_vecka.note: Web panel, 2,009 people aged 16+, Dec 2024–Feb 2025. 63% plan to strengthen their preparedness.

dryck_hemma_en_vecka.name: Have drinks/water at home for at least one week
dryck_hemma_en_vecka.note: 8,108 responses, December 2025. 61% have food for at least one week – water is the weakest link in household preparedness.

kontant_senaste_kop.name: Paid in cash at their most recent purchase
kontant_senaste_kop.note: 10% in 2023 and 40% in 2010. Low cash use increases vulnerability when digital payments are disrupted.

beredskapslager_livsmedel_budget.name: Government funding for emergency stockpiles in the food supply chain
beredskapslager_livsmedel_budget.note: Part of SEK 1,071 million for food and drinking water preparedness in 2026. Government food stockpiles are now being built up from virtually zero; a new law on emergency stockpiles is proposed to apply from 1 July 2026.

livsmedelsavfall_per_person_sverige.name: Food waste in the retail and consumer stages
livsmedelsavfall_per_person_sverige.note: 880,000 tonnes in total. Households account for 72%: 16 kg of avoidable food waste + 45 kg of other food waste per person. No reduction since 2020, despite an interim target of −20% by 2025.

skyfall_klimatfaktor_2071_2100_rcp85.name: Climate factor for cloudbursts 2071–2100 (RCP8.5 ≈ SSP5-8.5)
skyfall_klimatfaktor_2071_2100_rcp85.note: Short cloudbursts become about 40% more intense by 2071–2100 with RCP8.5 and about 20% with RCP4.5 (2041–2070: 20% and 15% respectively). Applies to all return periods and the whole country. Svenskt Vatten recommends at least 1.25 for rain shorter than one hour.

overdodlighet_varmebolja_2018.name: Excess mortality during the heatwave in summer 2018
overdodlighet_varmebolja_2018.note: About 700 more deaths than normal over the whole summer; SMHI cites 600–745 attributable to the heat. Mainly older people and the chronically ill were affected.

dodlighetsokning_varme_26c.name: Increase in mortality per day when it is at least 26 °C for three days in a row
dodlighetsokning_varme_26c.note: Mortality rises by about 10% per day at 26 °C or more three days in a row, and by a further 10% at 30 °C. Older people, the chronically ill and small children are most sensitive.

rvu_bil_andel_sverige.name: Car share of main trips in Sweden
rvu_bil_andel_sverige.note: Own calculation: 2,053 million car trips out of almost 3.9 billion main trips. Trafikanalys writes "just over half of all trips".

rvu_kollektiv_andel_sverige.name: Public transport modes' share of main trips in Sweden
rvu_kollektiv_andel_sverige.note: Own calculation: 708 million of approx. 3,900 million main trips. Increased by 5% from 2023 but is 10% below 2019.

rvu_gang_andel_sverige.name: Walking's share of main trips in Sweden
rvu_gang_andel_sverige.note: Own calculation: 499 million of approx. 3,900 million main trips. Walking trips fell by 9% from 2023 and are 20% below 2019.

rvu_cykel_andel_sverige.name: Cycling's share of main trips in Sweden
rvu_cykel_andel_sverige.note: Own calculation: 480 million of approx. 3,900 million main trips; +12% from 2023. Cycling accounts for only 2.2 of 137 billion kilometres travelled.

fritidsbatar_elmotor_andel_sverige.name: Motorboats with an electric motor
fritidsbatar_elmotor_andel_sverige.note: Share of motorboats with an electric motor (multiple answers possible): 4% for open motorboats, 2% for cabin boats. 17% still have a banned carburettor two-stroke engine. Measured in energy or traffic work, the electric share is much lower. A national measure: local data is lacking.

arbetstid_overenskommen.name: Agreed (contractual) mean working hours per week, employed aged 15–74
arbetstid_overenskommen.note: Margin of error ±0.1. Aged 20–64: 38.1 hours. Men 38.2 and women 36.2 hours (aged 15–74). Agreed weekly hours is the measure that best matches the model's "working time". Municipal figures are not available in the Labour Force Survey (AKU).

arbetstid_faktisk.name: Actual mean hours worked per week, employed aged 15–74
arbetstid_faktisk.note: Margin of error ±0.2. Average over all weeks of the year, so holiday, sickness and parental leave are counted. The measure therefore cannot be compared with an agreed 40-hour week. Aged 20–64: 30.6; men 31.6, women 27.7. In 2015: 30.1 hours.

deltid_andel.name: Employed with agreed working hours under 35 hours per week
deltid_andel.note: Own calculation: (277.8 + 601.9 thousand with 1–34 hours) / 5,263.0 thousand employed = 16.7%. Women 21.6%, men 12.3%. About 254 thousand lack agreed working hours; if they are excluded, the share becomes 17.6%.

sex_timmars_arbetsdag_stod.name: Share who think a six-hour working day is a good proposal
sex_timmars_arbetsdag_stod.note: The national SOM survey 2025: 55% good proposal, 22% neither, 23% bad proposal. Shows how large the support is for a reduction in working time.

hog_tillit_till_manniskor.name: High interpersonal trust (7–10 on a scale of 0–10)
hog_tillit_till_manniskor.note: The question reads: "to what extent can people in general be trusted?". 31% have medium (4–6) and 12% low (0–3) trust. A different measure from the yes/no question in the Health in Sweden survey (HLV), on which the model's trust is based.

ideellt_arbete_andel.name: Share who have done voluntary work in the past year, aged 16–84
ideellt_arbete_andel.note: Population study 2024. The share has been stable at 48–53% since 1992, with the most men and middle-aged people. According to SOM 2025, 34% are members of a sports or outdoor association, 40% of a trade union and 14% of a cultural association.

livsmedelsberedskap_planeringsmal_dagar.name: National planning target: food supply during a security-policy crisis (at least three months)
livsmedelsberedskap_planeringsmal_dagar.note: Food supply is to be secured "for at least three months where logistics flows with the outside world are limited" (90 days = own conversion). On 26 May 2026 the Riksdag adopted an act on emergency stockpiles in the food chain (SFS 2026:837), in force 1 July 2026. The first state grain stores are being built in Norrland during 2026. A target level, not a measured stock.

internet_icke_anvandare.name: Share of the population aged 16+ who do not use the internet
internet_icke_anvandare.note: Almost exclusively people of retirement age. 95% use e-ID, in practice mobile BankID, a single critical dependency. Almost one in four has refrained from booking a medical appointment because healthcare e-services are too difficult.

generativ_ai_anvandning.name: Share aged 16+ who have used generative AI tools
generativ_ai_anvandning.note: 25% in 2024. 18% use AI at work. 35% of companies used AI in 2025, and among large companies 72%.

kommuner_ai_i_alla_delar.name: Municipalities where AI is used to some extent in all parts of the operations
kommuner_ai_i_alla_delar.note: No municipality says that AI permeates the whole municipality. 40% use AI in some parts and 34% only among a few individuals. Barely one in four municipalities has an AI strategy (four in ten among municipalities with at least 50,000 inhabitants), and nearly half have guidelines. 7% have trained all staff. This is not an SKR survey, since none was found.

ai_forordningen_hogrisk_tillampning.name: Year the EU AI Act starts to apply to stand-alone high-risk systems (Annex III), 2 December
ai_forordningen_hogrisk_tillampning.note: The AI Act entered into force on 1 August 2024. Prohibitions and AI literacy have applied since 2 February 2025, GPAI rules since August 2025 and the rest of the regulation since 2 August 2026. The AI Omnibus (in force 27 July 2026) postponed the high-risk requirements to 2 December 2027 (Annex III, including public benefits) and 2 August 2028 (Annex I). Municipalities' AI in the exercise of public authority is mainly affected by Annex III.

konsumtion_kokvaxter_per_person.name: Consumption of fresh and frozen vegetables per person
konsumtion_kokvaxter_per_person.note: Total consumption, almost doubled since 1980. Direct consumption of fresh vegetables is 45.8 kg and of root vegetables 10.5 kg. Used as the denominator when calculating urban cultivation's share.

konsumtion_frukt_bar_per_person.name: Consumption of fresh and frozen fruit and berries per person
konsumtion_frukt_bar_per_person.note: Same level as in 1980. Including processed products (juice, jam and so on), consumption of fruit and berries is 82.4 kg per person per year.

utslapp_per_gastnatt.name: Climate impact per tourist guest night (West Sweden)
utslapp_per_gastnatt.note: Life-cycle calculation for tourism in West Sweden: 110 kg CO2e per tourist and 39 kg per guest night, of which travel to and from the destination is 54% and accommodation 23%.

ecodriving_bransle_besparing.name: Fuel saving from simulator-based eco-driving training (Kalmar Maritime Academy)
ecodriving_bransle_besparing.note: Courses for masters of small passenger ferries in the Stockholm archipelago have cut fuel use by up to 13%. Since 2015 more than 400 crew members on the Swedish Transport Administration's road ferries have been trained (1.5 litres less per crossing, a claimed 11,000 tonnes of CO₂ a year), and more than 700 officers in total. The figures are the simulator maker Kongsberg's account of a Linnaeus University report that has not been reviewed here.

unga_19_24_sverige_prognos_2050.name: Residents aged 19–24 in Sweden in 2050 according to Statistics Sweden's population projection
unga_19_24_sverige_prognos_2050.note: Sum of single-year ages 19–24 (own summation): 740,827 (2026), peaking at 779,316 (2035) and 667,595 (2050), i.e. −14% from the peak and −10% compared with 2026 (own calculations). Higher education's natural recruitment base grows until the mid-2030s and then shrinks, which sharpens competition for students.

befolkningstillvaxt_1ar.name: Population change, past year
befolkningstillvaxt_1ar.note: Change in population since the year before (Statistics Sweden). Sweden 0.168%, the county -0.176% (2025).

befolkningstillvaxt_5ar.name: Population change, past five years
befolkningstillvaxt_5ar.note: Change in population over the last five years (Statistics Sweden). Sweden 2.2%, the county -0.568% (2025).

befolkningstathet.name: Population density
befolkningstathet.note: Residents per square kilometre of land (Statistics Sweden). Sweden 25.9 inhabitants/km², the county 10.2 inhabitants/km² (2025).

andel_0_19.name: Share of inhabitants aged 0–19
andel_0_19.note: Share of the population aged 0–19 (Statistics Sweden). Sweden 22.4%, the county 21.6% (2025).

andel_65_plus.name: Share of inhabitants aged 65+
andel_65_plus.note: Share of the population aged 65 or over (Statistics Sweden). Sweden 21.1%, the county 26.4% (2025).

andel_80_plus.name: Share of residents aged 80 or older
andel_80_plus.note: 1,236 people; 9.4% in 2022. (The report's text says 13% for 2024, which does not match its own table.)

vaxthusgaser_per_inv.name: Territorial greenhouse gas emissions per inhabitant
vaxthusgaser_per_inv.note: Territorial emissions within the municipality (national emissions database, RUS/SMHI) – not consumption-based. Sweden 4.5 t CO2e per inhabitant, the county 5.5 t CO2e per inhabitant (2024).

vaxthusgaser_transporter_per_inv.name: Emissions from transport per inhabitant
vaxthusgaser_transporter_per_inv.note: Domestic transport within the municipality (RUS/SMHI). Sweden 1.6 t CO2e per inhabitant, the county 1.9 t CO2e per inhabitant (2024).

vaxthusgaser_jordbruk_per_inv.name: Emissions from agriculture per inhabitant
vaxthusgaser_jordbruk_per_inv.note: Farming's emissions: livestock digestion, manure and soils (RUS/SMHI). Sweden 0.585 t CO2e per inhabitant, the county 0.435 t CO2e per inhabitant (2024).

vaxthusgaser_el_fjarrvarme_per_inv.name: Emissions from electricity and district heating production per inhabitant
vaxthusgaser_el_fjarrvarme_per_inv.note: Emissions from the municipality's electricity and district-heating production (RUS/SMHI). Sweden 0.489 t CO2e per inhabitant, the county 0.370 t CO2e per inhabitant (2024).

vaxthusgaser_industri_per_inv.name: Emissions from industry per inhabitant
vaxthusgaser_industri_per_inv.note: Industry's combustion and process emissions (RUS/SMHI). Sweden 1.2 t CO2e per inhabitant, the county 2.0 t CO2e per inhabitant (2024).

elanvandning_per_inv.name: Final electricity use per inhabitant
elanvandning_per_inv.note: All final use of electricity in the municipality, industry included (Swedish Energy Agency/Statistics Sweden). Sweden 11.9 MWh per inhabitant, the county 18.3 MWh per inhabitant (2024).

fjarrvarme_fornybar_andel.name: Renewable share of district heating production
fjarrvarme_fornybar_andel.note: Share of the municipality's district-heating production from renewable sources (Swedish Energy Agency/Statistics Sweden). Sweden 83.9%, the county 88.2% (2024).

elproduktion_lokal.name: Electricity production within the municipality
elproduktion_lokal.note: All electricity produced within the municipality – hydro, wind, solar and combined heat and power (Swedish Energy Agency/Statistics Sweden).

solceller_installerad_effekt.name: Installed solar PV capacity
solceller_installerad_effekt.note: Grid-connected solar installations, installed capacity (Swedish Energy Agency).

vindkraft_installerad_effekt.name: Installed wind power capacity within the municipality
vindkraft_installerad_effekt.note: Installed capacity of wind turbines within the municipality (Swedish Energy Agency).

elbilar_andel.name: Share of electric cars in the passenger car fleet
elbilar_andel.note: Electric cars as a share of the cars in use (Transport Analysis). Sweden 8.6%, the county 4.3% (2025).

kollektivtrafiknara_lage.name: Population living close to public transport
kollektivtrafiknara_lage.note: Share with a stop with at least one departure an hour (weekdays 6–20) within 500 m as the crow flies. Sweden 80.9%, the county 75.6% (2024).

cykelvag_per_inv.name: Cycle paths per inhabitant
cykelvag_per_inv.note: Total length of cycle paths – municipal, state and private – per resident. Sweden 2.7 metres per inhabitant (2025).

ekologisk_akermark_andel.name: Organically farmed arable land
ekologisk_akermark_andel.note: Share of arable land farmed organically (Swedish Board of Agriculture). Sweden 14.1%, the county 21.2% (2025).

grundvatten_god_status.name: Groundwater bodies with good chemical and quantitative status
grundvatten_god_status.note: Share of groundwater bodies in good chemical and quantitative status (VISS/county boards). Sweden 97.2%, the county 99.7% (2022).

skyddad_natur_total.name: Protected nature, share of total area
skyddad_natur_total.note: National parks, nature reserves, nature conservation areas and biotope protection as a share of the total area (Statistics Sweden/Swedish EPA). Sweden 12.1%, the county 10.9% (2025).

medellivslangd_man.name: Life expectancy, men
medellivslangd_man.note: Life expectancy at birth, five-year average (Statistics Sweden). Sweden 81.8 years, the county 81.9 years (2025).

medellivslangd_kvinnor.name: Life expectancy, women
medellivslangd_kvinnor.note: Life expectancy at birth, five-year average (Statistics Sweden). Sweden 85.1 years, the county 84.9 years (2025).

sjalvskattad_god_halsa.name: Good self-rated health
sjalvskattad_god_halsa.note: Share aged 16–84 who rate their health good or very good (Public Health Agency's national survey, several years pooled). Sweden 71.0%, the county 70.1% (2024).

fetma.name: Obesity (BMI ≥ 30)
fetma.note: Share aged 16–84 with a BMI of 30 or more (national public health survey, several years pooled). Sweden 17.3%, the county 20.8% (2024).

fysiskt_aktiva.name: Physically active at least 150 min/week
fysiskt_aktiva.note: Share aged 16–84 physically active at least 150 minutes a week (national public health survey). Sweden 66.1%, the county 70.1% (2024).

allvarlig_psykisk_pafrestning.name: Serious psychological distress (adults 16–84)
allvarlig_psykisk_pafrestning.note: Share aged 16–84 with serious psychological distress on the Kessler 6 scale (national public health survey). Sweden 10.0%, the county 9.6% (2024).

psykisk_ohalsa_barn_unga.name: Mental ill health among children and young people aged 0–19
psykisk_ohalsa_barn_unga.note: Share aged 0–19 with a psychiatric diagnosis, psychotropic drugs or psychiatric care during the year (National Board of Health and Welfare). Sweden 10.0% (2024).

avsaknad_emotionellt_stod.name: Lack of emotional support (proxy for loneliness)
avsaknad_emotionellt_stod.note: Share aged 16–84 lacking emotional support – a measure close to loneliness (national public health survey). Sweden 13.3%, the county 13.1% (2024).

gymnasieexamen_4ar.name: Upper secondary diploma within 4 years
gymnasieexamen_4ar.note: Upper-secondary pupils registered in the municipality who graduate within four years, introductory programmes included (National Agency for Education). Sweden 74.8% (2025).

eftergymnasial_utbildning_25_64.name: Post-secondary education, ages 25–64
eftergymnasial_utbildning_25_64.note: Share aged 25–64 with post-secondary education (Statistics Sweden). Sweden 48.5%, the county 38.0% (2025).

arbetsloshet_20_64.name: Unemployment, ages 20–64 (BAS)
arbetsloshet_20_64.note: Register-based unemployment aged 20–64 in November (Statistics Sweden). Sweden 5.4%, the county 4.2% (2024).

unga_varken_arbetar_studerar.name: Young people aged 16–24 who are neither working nor studying
unga_varken_arbetar_studerar.note: Share aged 16–24 neither working nor studying (Statistics Sweden). Sweden 6.2%, the county 6.7% (2024).

medianinkomst_20_64.name: Median income (total earned income), ages 20–64
medianinkomst_20_64.note: Total earned income aged 20–64, median (Statistics Sweden). Sweden 401,400 SEK/year, the county 389,100 SEK/year (2024).

gini_disponibel_inkomst.name: Gini coefficient, disposable income
gini_disponibel_inkomst.note: Gini coefficient of households' disposable income; 0 is complete equality (Statistics Sweden). Sweden 0.314, the county 0.261 (2024).

barn_lag_ekonomisk_standard.name: Children and young people aged 0–19 with a low economic standard
barn_lag_ekonomisk_standard.note: Share aged 0–19 in households below 60% of the median economic standard (Statistics Sweden). Sweden 17.0%, the county 20.0% (2024).

nystartade_foretag_per_1000.name: New businesses per 1,000 inhabitants aged 16–64
nystartade_foretag_per_1000.note: New firms per 1,000 residents aged 16–64 (Growth Analysis). Sweden 11.5 number per 1,000, the county 10.5 number per 1,000 (2025).

trangboddhet_norm2.name: Overcrowding in multi-dwelling buildings (norm 2)
trangboddhet_norm2.note: Share living in blocks of flats with more than two people per room, kitchen and living room not counted (Statistics Sweden). Sweden 15.1%, the county 14.9% (2025).

fardigstallda_bostader_per_1000.name: Completed dwellings per 1,000 inhabitants
fardigstallda_bostader_per_1000.note: Dwellings completed by new building and conversion per 1,000 residents (Statistics Sweden). Sweden 3.1 dwellings per 1,000 inhabitants, the county 2.3 dwellings per 1,000 inhabitants (2025).

kvinnor_kommunfullmaktige.name: Share of women on the Municipal Council
kvinnor_kommunfullmaktige.note: Share of women among the municipal council's members this term (Statistics Sweden). Sweden 43.0% (2025).

avsaknad_tillit.name: Lack of trust in others
avsaknad_tillit.note: Share aged 16–84 answering no to whether most people can be trusted (national public health survey). Sweden 29.6%, the county 28.6% (2024).

otrygghet_kvall.name: Feel unsafe outdoors late in the evening in their own neighbourhood
otrygghet_kvall.note: Share who feel unsafe, or stay in, late at night in their own neighbourhood (Swedish Crime Survey); uncertain at municipal level. Sweden 25.0%, the county 21.2% (2025).

bredband_100mbit.name: Access to fixed broadband ≥ 100 Mbit/s
bredband_100mbit.note: Households with fixed broadband of at least 100 Mbit/s, or the immediate possibility, on 1 October (Post and Telecom Authority). Sweden 100% of households, the county 99.3% of households (2025).

kommunalt_avfall_kg_per_inv.name: Municipal waste collected per inhabitant
kommunalt_avfall_kg_per_inv.note: Municipal waste collected per resident, adjusted for holiday homes, tourism and commuting (Avfall Sverige). Sweden 424 kg per inhabitant, the county 422 kg per inhabitant (2025).

materialatervinning_andel.name: Municipal waste sent to material recycling, incl. biological treatment
materialatervinning_andel.note: Share of municipal waste collected for material recycling, biological treatment included (Avfall Sverige). The EU targets are 55% in 2025 and 65% in 2035. Sweden 40.0%, the county 41.5% (2025).

medborgare_nojda_dricksvattenarbete.name: Inhabitants who consider the municipality's work to secure drinking water to be good
medborgare_nojda_dricksvattenarbete.note: Share who think the municipality's work to secure drinking water is good (Statistics Sweden's citizen survey). Sweden 88.9%, the county 94.6% (2025).

vattenforekomster_god_status.name: Water bodies (all types) with good status
vattenforekomster_god_status.note: Share of the municipality's water bodies – lakes, rivers, coast and groundwater – in good status (VISS). Sweden 48.5%, the county 47.0% (2022).

medelavstand_skyddad_natur.name: Average distance to protected nature
medelavstand_skyddad_natur.note: Residents' average distance to the nearest protected nature area (Statistics Sweden). Sweden 2.0 km, the county 2.0 km (2025).

inpendling_antal.name: In-commuters to Rättvik Municipality
inpendling_antal.note: Employed people who work in the municipality but live in another (Statistics Sweden).

utpendling_antal.name: Out-commuters from Rättvik Municipality
utpendling_antal.note: Employed residents who work in another municipality (Statistics Sweden).

korstracka_personbil_per_inv.name: Distance driven by passenger car per inhabitant
korstracka_personbil_per_inv.note: Average distance driven by cars registered in the municipality, per resident (Transport Analysis). Sweden 625 mil/inhabitant/year, the county 725 mil/inhabitant/year (2024).

fossiloberoende_personbilar_andel.name: Fossil-independent passenger cars, share of the fleet
fossiloberoende_personbilar_andel.note: Electric, plug-in hybrid, gas, ethanol and other cars as a share of the cars in use (Transport Analysis). Sweden 26.0%, the county 20.4% (2025).

laddpunkter_publika_antal.name: Public charging points for electric cars
laddpunkter_publika_antal.note: Public charging points for electric cars in the municipality.

vaxthusgaser_transporter_ton.name: Greenhouse gas emissions from transport, total
vaxthusgaser_transporter_ton.note: Domestic transport emissions within the municipality, total (RUS/SMHI).

elproduktion_kraftvarme.name: Electricity production from combined heat and power
elproduktion_kraftvarme.note: Electricity from combined heat and power and industrial back-pressure within the municipality (Swedish Energy Agency/Statistics Sweden).

elproduktion_vindkraft.name: Electricity production from wind power within the municipality
elproduktion_vindkraft.note: Electricity from wind turbines within the municipality (Swedish Energy Agency/Statistics Sweden).

elproduktion_sol.name: Electricity production from solar power within the municipality
elproduktion_sol.note: Electricity from solar within the municipality (Swedish Energy Agency/Statistics Sweden).

bostadsmarknadslage_bme.name: Municipality's assessment of the housing market (0 = shortage, 1 = balance, 2 = surplus)
bostadsmarknadslage_bme.note: The municipality's own assessment in the National Board of Housing's survey: 0 shortage, 1 balance, 2 surplus.

bostadsmarknadslage_ungdomar_bme.name: Municipality's assessment of the housing market for young people aged 19–25 (0 = shortage)
bostadsmarknadslage_ungdomar_bme.note: The municipality's own assessment for 19–25-year-olds in the National Board of Housing's survey: 0 shortage, 1 balance, 2 surplus.

sysselsatta_arbetsstalle_kommun.name: Employed with a workplace in Rättvik Municipality
sysselsatta_arbetsstalle_kommun.note: Employed people with their workplace in the municipality, wherever they live (Statistics Sweden).

kommunen_tillsvidareanstallda.name: Permanently employed, monthly-paid staff in Rättvik Municipality
kommunen_tillsvidareanstallda.note: The municipality's permanent monthly-paid staff – people, not full-time equivalents (SKR).

trygg_i_skolan_ak8.name: Year 8 pupils who feel safe at school
trygg_i_skolan_ak8.note: Share of year-8 pupils who feel safe at school entirely or to a great extent.

individuellt_valbefinnande_index.name: Individual well-being, municipal index (0–100)
individuellt_valbefinnande_index.note: The Agency for Economic and Regional Growth's index of self-rated health, dental health and mental wellbeing, normalised across Sweden's municipalities (0–100). Sweden 55.2 (2025).

gott_psykiskt_valbefinnande.name: Inhabitants aged 16–84 with good mental well-being
gott_psykiskt_valbefinnande.note: Share aged 16–84 with good mental wellbeing (national public health survey, several years pooled). Sweden 84.9%, the county 85.4% (2024).

demografisk_forsorjningskvot.name: Demographic dependency ratio ((0–19 + 65+) / 20–64 years)
demografisk_forsorjningskvot.note: People aged 0–19 and 65+ per person aged 20–64 (Statistics Sweden): how many each person of working age supports. Sweden 0.770, the county 0.922 (2025).

ekologiska_livsmedel_kommunen.name: Organic food in the municipality's operations
ekologiska_livsmedel_kommunen.note: Organic food as a share of the municipality's food purchases by value (KRAV, Demeter, EU organic or MSC); contracted catering not included.

elproduktion_vattenkraft.name: Hydropower electricity generation in the municipality
elproduktion_vattenkraft.note: Hydropower supplied 16,106 MWh of the municipality's total generation of 104,671 MWh in 2024. The rest was wind (82,531 MWh) and solar (6,033 MWh); none came from combined heat and power. Output follows the water year: 9,776 MWh in 2022 and 20,855 MWh in 2019.

elanvandning_total.name: Total electricity use in the municipality
elanvandning_total.note: Final electricity use in all sectors, based on the grid companies' deliveries by municipality. The largest users are detached houses (46,653 MWh), industry (33,386 MWh), other services (21,306 MWh), the public sector (15,822 MWh) and holiday homes (15,138 MWh). Use has stayed between 129 and 155 GWh a year from 2010 to 2024.

lokal_elproduktion_andel_av_elanvandning.name: Local electricity generation relative to the municipality's electricity use
lokal_elproduktion_andel_av_elanvandning.note: 104,671 MWh generated / 139,830 MWh used = 74.9% (2023: 100,450 / 140,237 = 71.6%). This is an annual balance; hour by hour, power is bought and sold through the grid. The wind farm on Hedbodberget supplies about four fifths of local generation.

fjarrvarme_produktion.name: District heating production in the municipality
fjarrvarme_produktion.note: 45,813 MWh came from heat-only boilers and 10,633 MWh from flue-gas condensation. Fuel input was 55,964 MWh: 54,953 MWh solid biofuels, 580 MWh renewable oil and 431 MWh fossil oil (0.8%). The district heating produces no electricity, since there is no combined heat and power.

fjarrvarme_levererad.name: District heating delivered to end users
fjarrvarme_levererad.note: Apartment blocks 16,232 MWh, public sector 11,868 MWh, detached houses 9,519 MWh, other services 8,593 MWh and industry 1,297 MWh. Adven has run the network since 2020; it owns 51%, and Dala Energi and the municipality own 24.5% each. Adven states about 31 GWh a year and about 380 customers (500 connections) in central Rättvik, Boda and Vikarbyn. The gap to the SCB figure is unexplained.

fjarrvarme_andel_flerbostadshus.name: District heating's share of energy use in apartment blocks
fjarrvarme_andel_flerbostadshus.note: 16,232 MWh of district heating out of 19,164 MWh total energy use in apartment blocks = 84.7%. In detached houses the share is 10.7% (9,519 of 88,623 MWh). Detached houses are heated mainly with electricity (46,653 MWh) and wood, chips or pellets (32,276 MWh); SCB models the wood figure from the 2010 distribution.

slutlig_energianvandning_total.name: Total final energy use in the municipality
slutlig_energianvandning_total.note: All sectors and energy carriers in 2023; the total has stayed between 512 and 598 GWh a year since 2011. The 2024 total is confidential. The transport figures also have a break in the series in 2024 (a new model for oil deliveries), so 2023 is used.

industri_andel_slutlig_energianvandning.name: Industry's share of the municipality's final energy use
industri_andel_slutlig_energianvandning.note: 285,935 MWh in industry and construction / 598,329 MWh in total = 47.8% (2022: 42.2%). The fuel mix is confidential for 2023. For 2024, industry is shown using 149,386 MWh of fossil oil and 15,779 MWh of solid fossil fuels, probably mainly in SMA Mineral's lime works (see kalkverk_co2_fossil).

fossilfri_andel_slutanvandning_utom_indu.name: Fossil-free share of final energy use outside industry
fossilfri_andel_slutanvandning_utom_indu.note: Households, services, the public sector, agriculture and forestry, and transport used 312,395 MWh in 2023, of which 101,582 MWh was fossil fuel (95,390 MWh in transport): 1 − 101,582 / 312,395 = 67.5% (2022: 68.8%). Electricity and district heating count as fossil-free. Industry is left out because its fuels are confidential, so a renewable share for the whole municipality cannot be calculated.

transporter_fornybar_andel.name: Renewable share of transport energy, including electricity
transporter_fornybar_andel.note: (22,277 MWh renewable fuels + 473 MWh electricity) / 118,140 MWh = 19.3%; the rest is fossil petrol and diesel. The figure is based on deliveries to filling stations in the municipality, not on how far residents drive, and electricity used to charge electric cars is not included. 2023 is used because 2024 has a break in the series (260,362 MWh) and the biofuel blending mandate was lowered that year.

elanvandning_fritidshus.name: Electricity use in holiday homes
elanvandning_fritidshus.note: Holiday homes used 10.8% of the municipality's electricity in 2024 (15,138 of 139,830 MWh), about a third of what all year-round detached houses used (46,653 MWh). The figure shows Rättvik's role as a holiday-home area by Lake Siljan.

kalkverk_co2_fossil.name: Fossil CO2 emissions from SMA Mineral's lime works in Rättvik
kalkverk_co2_fossil.note: Reported emissions: 119,818 t in 2024, 87,761 t in 2023 and 120,418 t in 2022. Burning lime releases CO2 from the limestone itself, not only from the fuel, so switching fuel does not remove the emissions. SMA's other plant in the municipality, Boda lime works, has no CO2 data in the register.

broboberget_lannaberget_effekt.name: Planned wind power at Broboberget and Lannaberget: capacity in the grid connection agreement
broboberget_lannaberget_effekt.note: The permit covers up to 115 turbines (80 at Broboberget, 35 at Lannaberget), at most 230 m tall, about 50 km north-east of Rättvik on the border with Ovanåker, and became final on 27 May 2022 after appeals. Ellevio's agreement of 16 October 2023 covers up to 740 MW through a new 400 kV substation, with the first stage in 2027. No investment decision was found.

broboberget_lannaberget_produktion.name: Expected annual generation from Broboberget and Lannaberget
broboberget_lannaberget_produktion.note: wpd expects about 1.5 TWh a year, more than ten times the municipality's electricity use (139.8 GWh in 2024) and more than 14 times today's local generation (104.7 GWh). Part of the farms lies in Ovanåker municipality, and the split is not stated. The power is intended for industry's transition, including at SSAB and Ovako.

okat_behov_elnat_forbrukning_dalarna.name: Forecast increase in transmission capacity needed for electricity consumption in Dalarna up to 2034
okat_behov_elnat_forbrukning_dalarna.note: Ellevio's scenario 1 gives +57% for consumption and +129% for generation over 2025–2034, compared with the highest need since 2022, driven by electrification of industry, data centres and new power plants (peak load today about 800 MW). A weak margin in the national grid has forced Ellevio to stop connecting new large-scale generation in its Dalarna network until the Tandö substation is ready. Rättvik's local grid passed from Dala Energi to Sambygd AB in 2025 (Nordion Energi 51%, the municipality about 10%; annual report 2025, p. 19), and parts of northern Rättvik belong to Ellevio's Hälsingland network.

personbilar_per_1000_inv.name: Passenger cars in use per 1,000 inhabitants
personbilar_per_1000_inv.note: 7,465 passenger cars in use in 2025, or 679 per 1,000 inhabitants, against 598 in Dalarna and 475 in Sweden. Counting only cars owned by private individuals, the figure is 500 (Dalarna 480, Sweden 377); 1,967 cars are owned by companies and organisations. In 2015 the figure was 630.

utpendlare_leksand.name: Employed Rättvik residents working in Leksand municipality
utpendlare_leksand.note: The largest outbound commuting flow: of 5,191 employed Rättvik residents, 3,305 (63.7%) worked in their home municipality. In the other direction, 327 people commuted from Leksand to Rättvik. The train to Leksand takes 14–16 minutes.

utpendlare_falun.name: Employed Rättvik residents working in Falun municipality
utpendlare_falun.note: 173 people commuted from Falun to Rättvik, so 556 commute between the two in one direction or the other. This matches Region Dalarna's figure of 500–700 commuters between Falun and Rättvik. There is no direct train; the bus takes just under an hour.

utpendlare_mora.name: Employed Rättvik residents working in Mora municipality
utpendlare_mora.note: 167 people commuted from Mora to Rättvik. The train takes 23–25 minutes and runs 17 times each way on weekdays.

utpendlare_borlange.name: Employed Rättvik residents working in Borlänge municipality
utpendlare_borlange.note: 44 people commuted in the opposite direction. Another 70 Rättvik residents had their workplace in Stockholm municipality and 20 in Uppsala municipality; the register shows the workplace, not how often people travel there.

kollektivtrafik_marknadsandel.name: Public transport's share of motorised trips in Dalarna
kollektivtrafik_marknadsandel.note: The share of trips by bus and train among all trips by motor vehicle (walking and cycling excluded): 12% in 2019, 6% in 2021, 11% in 2023, 9% in 2024 and a provisional 7% for January–October 2025. The target is 12.5% in 2026 and 20% in 2035. No figure exists for Rättvik itself.

kollektivtrafik_vardagsresor_bra_andel.name: Share of residents who find public transport easy to use for everyday trips
kollektivtrafik_vardagsresor_bra_andel.note: 36.5% in 2025 (27.2% in 2023), against 44.4% in Dalarna and 68.8% in Sweden. 52.9% say it is easy to make longer trips without a car (N00574), and 18.0% say public transport works for leisure activities (N00573). This is a sample survey with a margin of error.

bilandel_resor_sverige.name: Car's share of main trips in Sweden
bilandel_resor_sverige.note: Own calculation: 2,052,673 of 3,872,529 thousand main trips = 53.0%; walking 12.9%, cycling 12.4% and public transport 18.3%. No travel survey for Rättvik or Dalarna was found. The share of kilometres travelled on foot, by bike or by public transport is highest in the big cities, so the car share in Rättvik is probably higher than the national figure.

restid_tag_stockholm_min.name: Fastest direct train Rättvik–Stockholm Central on a weekday
restid_tag_stockholm_min.note: SJ train 47 leaves Rättvik at 14:55 and reaches Stockholm Central at 18:16 (3 h 21 min); morning train 41 takes 3 h 26 min, and northbound train 48 is fastest at 3 h 15 min. With a change at Borlänge, the fastest trip takes 3 h 24 min (05:22–08:46). In the timetable from 13 December 2026, the direct trains become 1–9 minutes slower.

direkttag_stockholm_per_vardag.name: Direct trains Rättvik–Stockholm per weekday in each direction
direkttag_stockholm_per_vardag.unit: departures per weekday in each direction
direkttag_stockholm_per_vardag.note: SJ runs two trips a day between Mora and Stockholm Central via Borlänge, Uppsala and Arlanda (trains 41 and 47 southbound, 42 and 48 northbound) on an ordinary weekday in October–November 2026; on Sundays there are three. Other journeys need a change at Borlänge, where SJ has eight departures to Stockholm per weekday, and Masexpressen coaches take 3 h 40 min–3 h 55 min to the City Terminal. No night trains stop in Rättvik in the timetable data up to January 2027.

tag_avgangar_per_vardag.name: Train departures from Rättvik per weekday in each direction
tag_avgangar_per_vardag.unit: departures per weekday in each direction
tag_avgangar_per_vardag.note: On Wednesday 11 November 2026, 15 Tåg i Bergslagen regional trains (line 50 Morastrand–Borlänge; from December 2026 some continue to Sala) and 2 SJ trains run in each direction. Saturdays have 7 and Sundays 8 per direction. Region Dalarna counts 17 round trips Mora–Borlänge since December 2022, with 40–80 minutes between departures.

restid_tag_borlange_min.name: Train travel time Rättvik–Borlänge
restid_tag_borlange_min.note: The timetable gives 47 minutes by train, against 55 minutes by car according to Google, a travel-time ratio of 0.8. In autumn 2026 the trip takes 46–52 minutes. Borlänge is where passengers change for Stockholm, Falun and Gothenburg.

restid_tag_mora_min.name: Shortest train travel time Rättvik–Mora
restid_tag_mora_min.note: The trip takes 23–25 minutes, for example 10:08–10:31. Bus 350 takes 35–45 minutes. Mora is the main commuting destination in northern Dalarna, with many commuters from Rättvik and Orsa according to Region Dalarna.

restid_buss_falun_min.name: Bus travel time Rättvik–Falun
restid_buss_falun_min.note: Rättvik travel centre to Falun Knutpunkten takes 54 minutes by bus, against 45 minutes by car (travel-time ratio 1.20). Direct buses take 49 minutes (ratio 1.09). By train, passengers must change at Borlänge, and the trip then takes at least 83 minutes according to the autumn 2026 timetable data.

bussturer_falun_per_vardag.name: Bus trips Rättvik–Falun per weekday (line 350)
bussturer_falun_per_vardag.note: 20 departures towards Falun Monday–Friday (05:43–21:05) and 21 towards Mora; Saturdays and Sundays have 6 per direction, and some trips must be booked in advance. The express line 102 Rättvik–Borlänge ran until 16 June 2025. Line 351 Rättvik–Furudal has 13 trips per weekday in each direction.

restid_uppsala_borlange_efter_atgarder_m.name: Travel time Uppsala–Borlänge after the planned works on the Dalabanan line (around 2031)
restid_uppsala_borlange_efter_atgarder_m.note: Today's travel time is 100 minutes; works costing almost SEK 2 billion up to 2030 (passing loops that two trains can enter at once, new passing loops at Lustån and Heby, track renewal) are meant to cut it by about 7 minutes and make room for one long-distance train an hour. According to Region Dalarna, the regions' goal of 89 minutes needs works that do not fit in the 2026–2037 national plan. The whole line is single-track, and the Borlänge–Leksand–Rättvik–Mora section is called the Siljansbanan.

mal_restid_mora_stockholm_min.name: Regional target for train travel time Mora–Stockholm
mal_restid_mora_stockholm_min.note: The 2023–2025 regional plan sets a target of a Mora–Stockholm train link under three hours; today the direct train takes 3 h 40 min–3 h 51 min. The target is tied to 89 minutes Uppsala–Borlänge and needs faster trains with few stops and more capacity, and Region Dalarna writes that it should be worked out in a pre-study. An hourly Mora–Stockholm service is also to be studied.

mora_siljan_passagerare.name: Passengers at Mora–Siljan airport
mora_siljan_passagerare.note: 3,807 arriving and departing passengers in 2025, against 3,394 in 2024. In 2019 there were 2,838, and in 2018 4,701 (Transportstyrelsen, air traffic statistics 2019), after scheduled flights to Arlanda ended in February 2018. Since 2023, the route Sveg–Mora–Arlanda has been flown under a public service obligation.

dala_airport_passagerare.name: Passengers at Dala Airport in Borlänge
dala_airport_passagerare.note: 15,820 passengers in 2025, against 15,357 in 2024, 21,421 in 2019 and 26,456 in 2018 (Transportstyrelsen, air traffic statistics 2019). Borlänge is 46–52 minutes from Rättvik by train.

flyglinje_mora_arlanda_statligt_stod.name: State cost of the publicly procured air route Sveg–Mora–Arlanda
flyglinje_mora_arlanda_statligt_stod.note: Just over 9,000 passengers flew the route in 2025, which works out at about SEK 2,425 of state support per passenger; Mora accounts for about 4,000 passengers a year. In March 2026, Trafikverket proposed not to renew the public service obligation when the contracts end in October 2027. One reason is that the trip to Stockholm by other means takes under four hours from Mora.

bilandel_turistresor.name: Car's share of domestic tourist trips to Dalarna
bilandel_turistresor.note: The report says the car share is highest in Jönköping, Kalmar and Dalarna counties, at 91–92%, and lowest in Stockholm, at 43%, using data for 2017–2021; 91.5 is the midpoint. Nationally, the car's share of domestic tourist trips rose by 14 percentage points during the pandemic years. No figure for the Siljan area was found.

rv70_adt.name: Annual average daily traffic on national road 70 south of central Rättvik
rv70_adt.note: 8,698 vehicles a day (±7%), of which 468 are heavy or medium-heavy, according to a value valid from 1 January 2025. North of the centre, towards Mora, 9,349 vehicles a day pass (±12%, 2023), and on the one-way carriageways through the centre about 3,750–3,850 in each direction (2022). The map only shows annual averages; see rv70_adt_juli for summer.

rv70_adt_juli.name: Estimated daily traffic on national road 70 at Rättvik on an average July day
rv70_adt_juli.note: The annual average of 8,698 is made up of 8,230 light and 468 heavy vehicles; applying Trafikverket's July index for through routes (136.9 for cars, 113.8 for trucks) gives 8,230 × 1.369 + 468 × 1.138 ≈ 11,800. The tourist-road index gives ≈ 15,900, and the general state-road index ≈ 9,750. No summer count for Rättvik was found, and Classic Car Week at the end of July adds peaks on top of this.

temp_okning_2071_2100_rcp26.name: Increase in annual mean temperature by 2071–2100 vs 1971–2000, RCP2.6
temp_okning_2071_2100_rcp26.note: Ensemble mean of regional climate models (about 12×12 km) for the whole county; modelled 1971–2000 reference 2.9 °C (observed 3.0 °C). SMHI sub-area Siljan–Lower Österdalälven: +1.7 °C.

temp_okning_2071_2100_rcp45.name: Increase in annual mean temperature by 2071–2100 vs 1971–2000, RCP4.5
temp_okning_2071_2100_rcp45.note: Ensemble mean of regional climate models (about 12×12 km) for the whole county; modelled 1971–2000 reference 2.9 °C (observed 3.0 °C). Sub-area Siljan–Lower Österdalälven: +2.9 °C; winter (Dec–Feb) +3.9 °C.

temp_okning_2071_2100_rcp85.name: Increase in annual mean temperature by 2071–2100 vs 1971–2000, RCP8.5
temp_okning_2071_2100_rcp85.note: Ensemble mean of regional climate models (about 12×12 km) for the whole county; modelled 1971–2000 reference 2.9 °C (observed 3.0 °C). Sub-area Siljan–Lower Österdalälven: +4.8 °C; winter +6.2 °C, summer +4.5 °C.

hogsommardygn_1971_2000_lan.name: Hot days per year (daily maximum above 25 °C), observed mean 1971–2000
hogsommardygn_1971_2000_lan.note: Observation-based (gridded) county mean; the climate models' own reference for the same period is 6.6–6.7 days, which the scenario values should be compared with. The county mean is pulled down by the mountains – around Siljan the count is roughly twice as high (see hogsommardygn_1991_2020_lokal).

hogsommardygn_2071_2100_rcp26_lan.name: Hot days per year (daily maximum above 25 °C) 2071–2100, RCP2.6
hogsommardygn_2071_2100_rcp26_lan.note: County ensemble mean; an increase of 6.5 days on the modelled 1971–2000 reference (6.6 days). For the Siljan area, see the local estimates.

hogsommardygn_2071_2100_rcp45_lan.name: Hot days per year (daily maximum above 25 °C) 2071–2100, RCP4.5
hogsommardygn_2071_2100_rcp45_lan.note: County ensemble mean; an increase of 11.0 days on the modelled 1971–2000 reference (6.7 days). For the Siljan area, see the local estimates.

hogsommardygn_2071_2100_rcp85_lan.name: Hot days per year (daily maximum above 25 °C) 2071–2100, RCP8.5
hogsommardygn_2071_2100_rcp85_lan.note: County ensemble mean; an increase of 25.0 days on the modelled 1971–2000 reference (6.7 days). Mid-century (2041–2070): 18.8 days. For the Siljan area, see the local estimates.

hogsommardygn_2018_lan.name: Hot days in summer 2018 (daily maximum above 25 °C), observed
hogsommardygn_2018_lan.note: Observation-based county mean for 2018, the highest in the 1961–2018 series and on a par with the average year of 2071–2100 under RCP8.5 (31.7). SMHI's Leksand station had 46 such days that summer (own count).

hogsommardygn_1991_2020_lokal.name: Hot days per year (daily maximum above 25 °C) at Siljan, observed mean 1991–2020 (Leksand station)
hogsommardygn_1991_2020_lokal.note: Mean number of days above 25 °C per year at SMHI's Leksand station (172 m a.s.l., at Siljan's outlet, about 19 km from Rättvik), 27 complete years 1991–2020 (1992, 1993 and 2019 have gaps). The 1971–2000 mean was 14.0; Mora A had 14.5 (1991–2020). Hottest day in the series: 33.5 °C (1975).

hogsommardygn_2071_2100_rcp45_lokal.name: Hot days per year at Siljan 2071–2100, RCP4.5 (estimate)
hogsommardygn_2071_2100_rcp45_lokal.note: Leksand's observed 1971–2000 mean (14.0 days) plus the county's projected increase under RCP4.5 (+11.0 days) = 25 days. Additive scaling; proportional scaling would give more days, so the value is on the cautious side.

hogsommardygn_2071_2100_rcp85_lokal.name: Hot days per year at Siljan 2071–2100, RCP8.5 (estimate)
hogsommardygn_2071_2100_rcp85_lokal.note: Leksand's observed 1971–2000 mean (14.0 days) plus the county's projected increase under RCP8.5 (+25.0 days) = 39 days. Additive scaling; proportional scaling would give more days, so the value is on the cautious side.

langsta_period_hogsommardygn_2071_2100_r.name: Longest run of hot days (heat wave) 2071–2100, RCP8.5
langsta_period_hogsommardygn_2071_2100_r.note: The year's longest run of days with a maximum above 25 °C, county mean; observed 1971–2000: 3.6 days. RCP4.5 gives 6.6 and RCP2.6 5.3 days.

arsnederbord_forandring_2071_2100_rcp85.name: Change in annual precipitation by 2071–2100 vs 1971–2000, RCP8.5
arsnederbord_forandring_2071_2100_rcp85.note: SMHI gives +13 mm/month on the modelled reference of 61 mm/month for 1971–2000: 13/61 = 21%. RCP4.5 gives +9 mm/month (15%) and RCP2.6 +5 mm/month (8%).

vinternederbord_forandring_2071_2100_rcp.name: Change in winter precipitation (Dec–Feb) by 2071–2100, RCP8.5
vinternederbord_forandring_2071_2100_rcp.note: +15 mm/month on a modelled reference of 43 mm/month: 15/43 = 35%. RCP4.5: +9 mm/month (21%). A growing share falls as rain instead of snow.

sommarnederbord_forandring_2071_2100_rcp.name: Change in summer precipitation (Jun–Aug) by 2071–2100, RCP8.5
sommarnederbord_forandring_2071_2100_rcp.note: +9 mm/month on a modelled reference of 81 mm/month: 9/81 = 11%. RCP4.5: +8 mm/month (10%). Higher evaporation in warmer summers still makes drought more common (see soil moisture).

max_dygnsnederbord_forandring_2069_2098_.name: Change in the year's largest daily precipitation by 2069–2098 vs 1961–1990, RCP8.5
max_dygnsnederbord_forandring_2069_2098_.note: The county mean of the year's largest daily precipitation was 32 mm in 1961–1990 and is projected to rise by about 20% under RCP8.5, somewhat less under RCP4.5. For short cloudbursts SMHI uses a climate factor of about 1.2 (RCP4.5) and 1.4 (RCP8.5) by the end of the century.

vegetationsperiod_2071_2100_rcp45.name: Length of the growing season 2071–2100, RCP4.5
vegetationsperiod_2071_2100_rcp45.note: Days from the start of the growing season (daily mean above 5 °C four days running) to its end, county mean; observed 1971–2000: 157 days. RCP2.6 gives 176 and RCP8.5 217 days.

max_snovatteninnehall_forandring_2071_21.name: Change in the year's maximum snow pack (water equivalent) by 2071–2100, RCP8.5
max_snovatteninnehall_forandring_2071_21.note: Applies to SMHI's sub-area Siljan–Lower Österdalälven, where the modelled maximum snow water equivalent was 71 mm in 1971–2000; the decrease is 47% under RCP4.5. Less snow means a smaller spring flood but more rain-driven floods in autumn and winter.

dagar_lag_markfuktighet_2069_2098_rcp85.name: Days per year with low soil moisture at the end of the century (2069–2098), RCP8.5
dagar_lag_markfuktighet_2069_2098_rcp85.note: SMHI gives 30–40 days a year of low soil moisture for most of the county under RCP8.5 (20–25 under RCP4.5), against 5–10 days today; the value is the middle of the range. It is a drought index for irrigation need and fire risk.

istacke_dagar_2016_2026.name: Length of the ice season on Siljan (Storsiljan), mean of winters 2015/16–2025/26
istacke_dagar_2016_2026.note: Mean number of days between freeze-up and break-up for the ten winters with observations (2019/20 missing). In 1871–1900 the mean was 129 days and break-up came on average on 7 May, against 9 April in 2016–2026; in winter 2024/25 the ice lay for only 35 days.

siljan_medelvattenstand.name: Mean water level of Siljan 1964–2024
siljan_medelvattenstand.note: Mean level under the current water-court ruling, measured at Byrviksbanken (Siljansnäs). Mean low water 160.07 and mean high water 161.98 m; before regulation (1900–1925) the mean was 161.0 m. Add about 0.4 m for RH 2000 (see hojdskillnad_rh2000_rh1900).

siljan_dammningsgrans.name: Siljan's upper regulation limit under the 1964 water-court ruling
siljan_dammningsgrans.note: The ruling (AD 45/1947, 27 Feb 1964) allows regulation between +159.90 and +161.78 m – an amplitude of 1.88 m – from Gråda power station about 20 km downstream of Leksand. Above the limit, releases must follow the natural discharge: 293 m³/s at +161.78 and about 2 m³/s more per cm.

siljan_hogsta_vattenstand_1985.name: Siljan's highest level since the current regulation (13 September 1985)
siljan_hogsta_vattenstand_1985.note: Peak after a very wet summer and autumn; Siljan rose a metre in a week, during the same rains that breached the Noppikoski dam. Next highest: 162.90 (Nov 2000), 162.73 (June 1995) and 162.62 (Aug 2023). About +163.4 m in RH 2000.

siljan_hogsta_kanda_vattenstand_1860.name: Siljan's highest known water level (1860)
siljan_hogsta_kanda_vattenstand_1860.note: The county board states that the highest known level before regulation was 3.25 m above the 161.78 m limit: 161.78 + 3.25 = 165.03 m. SMHI dates the record to 1860, about two metres above the 1985 level; the highest level in 1900–1925 was 163.9 m.

siljan_hogvatten_2023.name: Siljan's peak level after storm Hans (18 August 2023)
siljan_hogvatten_2023.note: According to SMHI the highest level since 2000 and the highest August level since regulation began in 1964; the peak came on 18 August in SMHI's daily Byrviksbanken series. Of the four highest levels since 1964, three followed summer or autumn rain (1985, 2000, 2023) and one an early-summer flood (1995).

siljan_andel_ar_over_dammningsgrans.name: Share of years in which Siljan rose above the +161.78 m regulation limit, 1967–2025
siljan_andel_ar_over_dammningsgrans.note: The annual maximum exceeded +161.78 m in 40 of 59 years (1967–2025); in 1991–2020 in 17 of 30 years, in line with the county board's 'on average every other year'. Siljan has risen more than a metre above the limit (+162.78) twice: 1985 and 2000.

siljan_utflode_100ar_idag.name: 100-year outflow from Siljan at Gråda power station, present climate
siljan_utflode_100ar_idag.note: Gråda power station controls Siljan's outlet. The 200-year flow is 655 m³/s and the design (probable maximum) flood 1,405 m³/s. MSB's climate-adjusted 100-year flow for 2098 is lower, 490 m³/s, because the spring flood shrinks in the scenarios used then; SMHI's newer projections point to an increase instead (see siljan_hogflode_50ar_forandring_2071_2100_rcp85).

siljan_100arsniva_idag.name: Siljan's 100-year level in the present climate (estimate)
siljan_100arsniva_idag.note: The water-court discharge table gives 612 m³/s (MSB's 100-year flow at Gråda) at +163.30 m; the table matches SMHI's observations (163.04 m and about 570 m³/s in 1985). About +163.7 m in RH 2000; no official 100-year level for Siljan was found published in text.

siljan_hogflode_50ar_forandring_2071_210.name: Change in the 50-year flow out of the Siljan area by 2071–2100, RCP8.5 (current regulation)
siljan_hogflode_50ar_forandring_2071_210.note: Applies to the outlet of SMHI's sub-area Siljan–Lower Österdalälven (modelled 465 m³/s in 1971–2000). RCP4.5 gives +9.9% and RCP2.6 +11.8%; the 10-year flow rises 15% (RCP8.5). MSB's older calculation (2013) points to a decrease instead, so the direction is uncertain.

siljan_100arsniva_2071_2100_rcp85.name: Siljan's 100-year level 2071–2100, RCP8.5 (estimate)
siljan_100arsniva_2071_2100_rcp85.note: 612 m³/s × 1.132 = 693 m³/s, which the water-court discharge table puts at +163.63 m (RCP4.5: 673 m³/s, +163.55 m). About +164.0 m in RH 2000 – level with Rättvik's lowest lakeside streets. With MSB's flow for 2098 (490 m³/s) the level would instead be +162.76 m.

hojdskillnad_rh2000_rh1900.name: Difference between the RH 2000 and RH 1900 height systems at Siljan (estimate)
hojdskillnad_rh2000_rh1900.note: In Lantmäteriet's terrain model Siljan's surface at Rättvik lies at +162.18 m (RH 2000); the tile was laser-scanned on 6 November 2020, the day SMHI measured +161.78 m (RH 1900) at Byrviksbanken. Difference about 0.40 m (uncertainty about ±0.15 m); used to convert SMHI's Siljan levels to RH 2000.

lagsta_strandgata_niva.name: Lowest street level by Siljan and the lowest reach of Enån in Rättvik
lagsta_strandgata_niva.note: Lowest point along the streets nearest the water: Badhusgatan +164.04 and Båthamnsvägen +164.12 m (4 m grid, OSM street centre lines). About +163.6 m in RH 1900 – some 2.4 m above Siljan's mean level and 0.6 m above the 1985 record; the square and the station lie at about +166 m.

byggnader_under_100arsniva.name: Buildings in central Rättvik with ground below Siljan's estimated 100-year level (+163.7 m RH 2000)
byggnader_under_100arsniva.note: Buildings (OSM, about 2.9 × 2.9 km around the centre) whose lowest corner lies below +163.7 m RH 2000, 7 of them within 150 m of Siljan or the lake-affected lower reach of Enån – mainly houses around Badhusgatan–Knihsgatan by Enån, a shed at Enån's mouth and a shop building at the campsite. Below +164.0 m: 19 buildings; below +165.0 m: 62.

camping_andel_under_100arsniva.name: Share of Siljanbadet campsite's ground below Siljan's estimated 100-year level (+163.7 m RH 2000)
camping_andel_under_100arsniva.note: Share of the campsite's 9.1 ha (OSM polygon) with ground below +163.7 m RH 2000 (estimated 100-year level today); below +164.0 m (estimated 100-year level 2071–2100, RCP8.5): 57%. The campsite and beach are Rättvik's lowest-lying developed land.

lagsta_grundlaggningsniva_siljan.name: Lowest foundation level for new buildings at Siljan's outlet (Leksand municipality)
lagsta_grundlaggningsniva_siljan.note: Leksand's comprehensive plan (2014) sets +165 m a.s.l. as the lowest foundation level for new buildings by Österdalälven/Siljan's outlet, based on the 10,000-year flood; the Limsjöänget detailed plan in Leksand uses +165 m in RH 2000. No equivalent published level for Rättvik was found.

skyfall_2023_skadade_villor.name: Houses damaged by cloudbursts and flooding in August 2023 (storm Hans)
skyfall_2023_skadade_villor.note: Local cloudbursts on 6–8 August 2023 damaged about 150 houses in Lerdal, Gärdebyn, Söderås, Utby and parts of central Rättvik (homes on steep slopes down to Siljan); about 25 km of road was wholly or partly destroyed and the rail embankment at Tällberg was washed away. Rättvik has no SMHI station of its own; Leksand got 145 mm from 30 July to 10 August.

dimensionerande_skyfall_100ar_2h.name: Design cloudburst in Rättvik's cloudburst mapping: 100-year rain, 2 hours, including climate factor
dimensionerande_skyfall_100ar_2h.note: The cloudburst mapping of the water and sewerage facilities (Scalgo LIVE) used a 2-hour 100-year rain with a climate factor of 1.2 (72 mm; 40 mm after deducting pipe and infiltration capacity) and a 500-year rain with a climate factor of 1.35 (149 mm). It found 11 risk sites, all sewage pumping stations, four of them in a higher risk class; storm water is not treated today.

vattentakt_tillstand_max_dygn.name: Permitted maximum groundwater abstraction at the Gärdsjö source (Rättvik's main supply)
vattentakt_tillstand_max_dygn.note: The permit for the municipality's abstraction just west of lake Gärdsjön allows at most 4,500 m³/day and 1.46 million m³/year (about 4,000 m³/day on average). The source lies in the Gärdsjöfältet water-supply interest (protection zones Jutjärn Boda, Rättvik, Västanå); a new well field and a new Gärdsjö water works came into service in 2025, and the water is only aerated and UV-treated.

andel_egen_brunn.name: Share of the municipality's residents with their own well
andel_egen_brunn.note: The municipality says 'close to 40%' of the population has its own dug or drilled well; for Dalarna county as a whole about 20% had private supply in 2020 (county board, Statistics Sweden). The municipality is not responsible for quality; uranium and radon occur in drilled wells.

siljan_ekologisk_status.name: Ecological status of Siljan (VISS)
siljan_ekologisk_status.note: Moderate ecological status, mainly because of fish and connectivity (dams and regulation – the eel has vanished and the Siljan brown trout has fallen from thousands to a few hundred); nutrients, light conditions and phytoplankton have high status. Chemical status: not good (mercury, PBDE). Target: good ecological status by 2033; Enån through Rättvik has good ecological status.

siljansbadet_prov_algblomning.name: Bathing-water samples with algal bloom at Siljansbadet 2023–2026
siljansbadet_prov_algblomning.note: None of 26 samples at the EU bathing site Siljansbadet in 2023–2026 showed an algal bloom, and the bathing profile lists no cyanobacteria risk – Siljan is nutrient-poor. Classification: excellent 2023–2024, good 2025; one sample on 7 July 2026 was unfit (bacteria) and the sample on the day of storm Hans (8 Aug 2023) was flagged.

folkmangd_kommun.name: Population of Rättvik Municipality, 31 December
folkmangd_kommun.note: Down 20 from 10,998 in 2024. More deaths than births, but more people move in than out.

folkmangd_prognos_2034.name: Municipal population forecast for 2034
folkmangd_prognos_2034.note: The municipality's own projection: from 10,998 residents in 2024 to 10,965 in 2034.

folkmangd_tatort.name: Population of Rättvik town (urban area)
folkmangd_tatort.note: Statistics Sweden urban-area delineation 2023 (code 2031TC106). Density 438 residents per km².

folkmangd_tatort_1960.name: Population of Rättvik town in 1960
folkmangd_tatort_1960.note: The town grew from 3,140 residents in 1960 to 5,369 in 2023.

tatort_landareal.name: Land area of Rättvik town
tatort_landareal.note: Land area inside the 2023 urban-area boundary. The model square (1.7 × 1.7 km ≈ 289 ha) covers the central part.

kommun_yta.name: Area of the municipality
kommun_yta.note: About the size of Lake Vättern. It covers the parishes of Rättvik, Boda and Ore.

forsorjningskvot.name: Demographic dependency ratio
forsorjningskvot.note: Residents outside ages 20–64 per resident aged 20–64. Among the highest in Sweden; up from 0.99 ten years ago.

forsorjningskvot_dalarna.name: Demographic dependency ratio, Dalarna County
forsorjningskvot_dalarna.note: County average as given in the municipal annual report.

forsorjningskvot_riket.name: Demographic dependency ratio, Sweden
forsorjningskvot_riket.note: National average as given in the municipal annual report.

okning_85_89_till_2034.name: Change in the number of people aged 85–89 by 2034
okning_85_89_till_2034.note: +287 people in the municipal forecast, the age when care needs rise most. Aged 90+: +53% (+110).

forandring_barn_6_12_till_2034.name: Change in the number of children aged 6–12 by 2034
forandring_barn_6_12_till_2034.note: −61 children in the municipal forecast; ages 1–5 −8% (−36), ages 16–19 −4% (−19).

andel_20_64.name: Share of residents of working age (20–64)
andel_20_64.note: 5,252 people per the population table; the goal is a larger working-age share. (The goals section of the same report says 47.2%.)

skatter_statsbidrag_budget.name: Tax revenue, general state grants and equalisation, budget
skatter_statsbidrag_budget.note: Of which own tax revenue about SEK 604 million.

resultatmal.name: Financial target: annual surplus relative to taxes and grants
resultatmal.note: Target for 2026–2028. Budgeted 2026 surplus SEK 17.98 million.

resultat_2025.name: Municipal result (surplus)
resultat_2025.note: Includes a one-off capital gain of SEK 311 million from redeeming shares in Dala Energi.

resultat_2025_exkl_reavinst.name: Result excluding the capital gain, share of taxes and grants
resultat_2025_exkl_reavinst.note: SEK 14.7 million. Below the 2% target; operations do not fully stay within budget.

dala_energi_reavinst.name: Capital gain from redeeming Dala Energi shares
dala_energi_reavinst.note: The municipality redeemed half of its 5.2 million shares and bought about 10% of Sambygd AB (power and fibre grids).

soliditet_inkl_pension.name: Equity ratio including pension obligations
soliditet_inkl_pension.note: Without the capital gain it would have been 32.4%.

soliditet_mal_2028.name: Target equity ratio including pension obligations
soliditet_mal_2028.note: To be reached by the end of 2028.

koncern_laneskuld_per_invanare.name: Long-term debt of the municipal group per resident
koncern_laneskuld_per_invanare.note: SEK 1,239 million in total. National average about SEK 78,000 per resident in 2024. The rise comes mainly from water and sewage investment.

koncern_langfristig_laneskuld.name: Long-term debt of the municipal group
koncern_langfristig_laneskuld.note: Up SEK 129 million in 2025, mainly in the water and waste company. Interest-bearing debt was SEK 1,173 million (the budget document says 1,171).

investeringsbudget.name: Municipal capital budget
investeringsbudget.note: Includes the toboggan run SEK 8m, Toppstugan SEK 7m, beach toilets SEK 2m, Långbryggan SEK 0.5m and Enån beach infrastructure SEK 0.3m.

socialforvaltning_andel_ramar.name: Social services' share of the operating budget
socialforvaltning_andel_ramar.note: Education has 35.0%; together almost 80% of the budget.

socialforvaltning_underskott.name: Social services budget deviation
socialforvaltning_underskott.note: −1.5% of budget. The 2024 overrun was SEK 24 million; recovery is expected to take 3–5 years.

lokala_ambitioner_antal.name: Number of local sustainability ambitions (Agenda 2030)
lokala_ambitioner_antal.note: Local ambitions for a sustainable Rättvik, adopted 26 Sep 2024. The work began in 2016 when UNDP visited Rättvik, the first Swedish municipality.

fossilfritt_transportsystem_mal.name: Goal: fossil-free transport system in the municipality
fossilfritt_transportsystem_mal.note: Local sub-goal: the municipality's transport system is to be fossil-free by 2030. The value 100% is our restatement of the goal.

energianvandning_lokaler.name: Energy use in municipal buildings per heated area

hvo_andel_fordon.name: Share of municipal vehicles fuelled with HVO100
hvo_andel_fordon.note: The municipality has no electric vehicles and does not measure emissions.

ny_solel_ansluten.name: Solar power connected to the grid in the municipality
ny_solel_ansluten.note: Up 21% (1.20 MW) from 5.79 MW in 2023, per the annual report.

vindkraft_antal_verk.name: Number of wind turbines in the municipality
vindkraft_antal_verk.note: Unchanged for 13 years per the Swedish Energy Agency.

vindkraft_effekt.name: Installed wind power capacity in the municipality
vindkraft_effekt.note: 15 turbines; in Dalarna each MW yields about 2.5 GWh a year.

vindkraftsstod.name: State wind power grant to the municipality 2025–2026
vindkraftsstod.note: All of it goes to local associations. From 2027 about SEK 0.5–0.6 million a year is expected.

lokalproducerade_livsmedel.name: Share of locally produced food in municipal kitchens
lokalproducerade_livsmedel.note: Up from 30% in 2024. Food meeting organic criteria: 34%.

andel_ravaror_atertaget.name: Share of produce from the agricultural school ('Återtaget') in public kitchens
andel_ravaror_atertaget.note: Meat, potatoes and grain from the school farm; 21% the year before.

gymnasieexamen_3ar.name: Share graduating upper secondary within three years, Stiernhööksgymnasiet

ak9_betyg_alla_amnen.name: Share of year-9 pupils with passing grades in all subjects
ak9_betyg_alla_amnen.note: Down from 74.4% in 2024 (National Agency for Education).

behorighet_gymnasiet.name: Share of pupils eligible for national upper-secondary programmes

grundskolor_antal.name: Number of municipal compulsory schools
grundskolor_antal.note: Nyhedsskolan (years F–6, ~230 pupils) and Rättviksskolan (years 7–9, 250+) are in town; the smallest, Sätra, has about 10 pupils.

satra_skola_elever.name: Pupils at Sätra school (years F–3)
satra_skola_elever.note: The municipality says 'about 10 pupils'; the school is 4 km from central Rättvik.

grundskola_elever_summa.name: Pupils in municipal compulsory schools, sum of approximate figures
grundskola_elever_summa.note: Our own calculation: the sum of the rounded pupil numbers ('about', 'just over') given for the eight schools.

naturbruk_forstahandssokande.name: First-choice applicants to the agriculture track
naturbruk_forstahandssokande.note: 42 first-choice applications for 24 places. The school farm has bought a dairy to be installed in Rättvik.

sjukfranvaro.name: Total sick leave among municipal employees

tillsvidareanstallda.name: Permanent municipal employees
tillsvidareanstallda.note: Average age 47.0; 47.6% are 50 or older. Many retirements are expected among teachers, managers and assistant nurses.

naringslivsranking.name: Rank in the Confederation of Swedish Enterprise business climate ranking
naringslivsranking.note: Down 22 places from 50th in 2024; the goal was to improve by 10.

bostader_mal_per_ar.name: Goal: new homes per year
bostader_mal_per_ar.note: Housing programme 2020–2030: at least 30 new homes a year through work with property owners.

smahustomter_till_maklare.name: Plots for detached houses handed to estate agents
smahustomter_till_maklare.note: The goal was at least four plots.

utsikten_tomter.name: Housing plots in the 'Utsikten' detailed plan (Lerdal)
utsikten_tomter.note: Adopted 11 June 2026. Plots can be merged for small blocks of flats; a storm pond is sized for a 100-year rain plus a 30% climate factor.

rfab_underhall_budget.name: Maintenance budget of the municipal housing company
rfab_underhall_budget.note: The company says SEK 120–130/m² is needed to avoid emergency repairs, despite a 7% rent rise in 2025.

va_ledningsnat.name: Length of water and sewer pipes
va_ledningsnat.note: 'About 600 km', largely built 1955–1979 and in need of renewal.

va_anslutna_anlaggningar.name: Properties connected to public water and sewage
va_anslutna_anlaggningar.note: Active subscriptions in May 2024; six water sources and five treatment plants.

va_skyfall_riskplatser.name: Water and sewage facilities at risk in cloudbursts
va_skyfall_riskplatser.note: All are sewage pumping stations; four are higher risk. Stormwater is not treated today.

rvab_investeringar.name: Investment by the municipal water and waste company
rvab_investeringar.note: Including sewer extension in Backa (forecast SEK 79m) and the Furudal–Kärvsåsen transfer pipe (forecast SEK 32.2–35.2m).

va_brukningsavgift_hojning_2026.name: Increase in water and sewage usage charges
va_brukningsavgift_hojning_2026.note: Council decision 7 May 2026; connection fees unchanged. The Sweden Democrats dissented.

va_brukningsavgift_hojning_2025.name: Increase in water and sewage usage charges from 1 April 2025
va_brukningsavgift_hojning_2025.note: Equal to 15% on an annual basis.

siljan_hogsta_vattenstand_reglerad.name: Highest water level of Lake Siljan under the current water court ruling
siljan_hogsta_vattenstand_reglerad.note: Period 1964–2024. Before regulation (1900–1925) the maximum was 163.9 m; the mean is 161.18 m. Height system as given by SMHI.

siljan_vattendom_ovre_grans.name: Upper regulation limit for Lake Siljan
siljan_vattendom_ovre_grans.note: 1964 water court ruling: the level is to stay between 159.9 and 161.78 m, with special rules in spring floods. Regulated at Gråda power plant (1951).

lerdalsberget_naturreservat.name: Lerdalsberget nature reserve
lerdalsberget_naturreservat.note: Decided 7 May 2026; the municipality's third own reserve, old forest close to town.

vardcentral_kopesumma.name: Municipal purchase of the health centre building
vardcentral_kopesumma.note: Council decision Dec 2023. The building houses the health centre and the Prästskogen care home; it was bought partly to make room for a family centre, which opened around the turn of 2025/2026.

kf_mandat_c_m_kd.name: Seats held by the outgoing Centre–Moderate–Christian Democrat coalition
kf_mandat_c_m_kd.note: Our own sum (8 + 8 + 2) of 39 seats; the coalition held 20 in 2022–2026 and has lost its majority.

ccw_bilar.name: Cars during Classic Car Week
ccw_bilar.note: 'Around ten thousand cars and many more people' each year; held in week 31.

ccw_startar.name: Classic Car Week first held
ccw_startar.note: Planning began in spring 1991; held every year in week 31 since.

langbryggan_langd.name: Length of Långbryggan pier
langbryggan_langd.note: Measured from the shore to the steamer quay. Poet Bo Bergman called it 'almost as long as eternity'.

langbryggan_byggd.name: Långbryggan built
langbryggan_byggd.note: Landing for the steamer S/S Rättvik, in service on Siljan from 1895 to the 1950s.

langbryggan_namnplankor.name: Name planks sold to fund the Långbryggan renovation
langbryggan_namnplankor.note: The public and firms bought engraved planks to fund the renovation; reopened 6 June 1992. Wikipedia says 2,638.

sandstrand_langd.name: Sandy beach in central Rättvik
sandstrand_langd.note: The municipality lists '1,200 metres of sandy beach' in central Rättvik. In OSM, the Siljansbadet bathing place and campsite lie on the beach north of the pier.

kyrkstallar_antal.name: Church stables at Rättvik church
kyrkstallar_antal.note: In two groups, mostly 18th–19th century. Kyrkudden is a cultural heritage area of national interest (W89).

kyrkstall_aldsta.name: Oldest church stable by tree-ring dating
kyrkstall_aldsta.note: The heritage programme gives 1492; the municipal website says the 1470s.

kyrka_takstolar_aldsta.name: Nave roof trusses, earliest tree-ring date
kyrka_takstolar_aldsta.note: The 27 nave roof trusses date from 1354–1367. The municipality says the church dates back to the 1200s.

kyrka_exterior.name: Current exterior of Rättvik church
kyrka_exterior.note: Extended several times; the present exterior dates from 1793.

kyrkklocka_aldsta.name: The great bell of Rättvik church
kyrkklocka_aldsta.note: Dalarna's oldest set of three bells: 1593, 1622 and 1628.

vasa_tal_ar.name: Gustav Vasa's first speech to the Dalecarlians at Rättvik church
vasa_tal_ar.note: By tradition and the inscription on Vasastenen, December 1520; in January 1521 King Christian's troops were defeated at the church.

vasastenen_rest.name: Vasastenen monument raised
vasastenen_rest.note: A memorial stone with three shields and red dragon bands, ringed by twelve smaller stones for Vasa's helpers.

stiernhook_fodd.name: Jurist Johan Stiernhöök born in Rättvik
stiernhook_fodd.note: Born at Hökbacken, died 1675; called 'the father of Swedish jurisprudence'. The council meets in the Stiernhöök hall.

rattvik_egen_socken.name: Rättvik becomes its own parish
rattvik_egen_socken.note: In the early 1300s the area belonged to Leksand parish; around 1325 it became a parish of its own.

kyrkbat_aldsta_siljan.name: Year carved on the oldest church boat on Siljan
kyrkbat_aldsta_siljan.note: Big boats with 8–12 pairs of oars; Rättvik's oldest known church boat 'Aros' was used until 1905. 'Sörbyggarn' was built in 1950.

rattviksmaleriet_start.name: Rättvik folk painting emerges (decade)
rattviksmaleriet_start.note: The Rättvik painting style emerged in the 1760s; the crop failures of 1771–1773 sent painters on work journeys.

emigranter_1864_1889.name: Emigrants from Rättvik 1864–1889
emigranter_1864_1889.note: 'Nearly one thousand' per Robert Ostergren's study; almost half settled in Isanti County (Minnesota) or Clay County (Dakota). The first family left in 1864.

emigranter_vastbjorka_1860tal.name: Emigrants from Västbjörka village in the 1860s
emigranter_vastbjorka_1860tal.note: 'Over 70 people' emigrated and some farms disappeared entirely.

jarnvag_oppnad.name: The railway reaches Rättvik
jarnvag_oppnad.note: Sågmyra–Rättvik opened 12 August 1890; Rättvik–Mora on 2 August 1891.

stationshus_byggt.name: Current station building in Rättvik
stationshus_byggt.note: Replaced the c.1890 building. Rättvik became a junction in 1914; the Falun line closed in 1965.

lokstallarna_byggd.name: The locomotive sheds built
lokstallarna_byggd.note: Used to service engines and carriages for most of the 1900s; renovated and reopened as a venue in 2025.

gustaf_wasa_byggd.name: Steamer Gustaf Wasa launched on Siljan
gustaf_wasa_byggd.note: Launched 29 April 1876 and on Siljan ever since; a listed historic vessel for 140 passengers that calls at Långbryggan.

municipalsamhalle.name: Rättvik becomes a 'municipal community'
municipalsamhalle.note: Founded 25 November 1910, giving the station town its own administration for fire safety and health.

hotell_siljansborg.name: Tourist hotel Siljansborg completed
hotell_siljansborg.note: Persborg opened in 1903. King Gustav V rented Siljansborg for some weeks in 1911 and 1912; waitresses wore folk costume. Both hotels are gone.

vidablick_invigd.name: Vidablick lookout tower opened
vidablick_invigd.note: Opened 12 June 1898 on Hedsåsberget, 252 m above Siljan; designed by 17-year-old Olof Klockars. Outside the 3D model.

kommunalhus_invigt.name: Court and town hall opened
kommunalhus_invigt.note: Designed by Artur von Schmalensee and built 1951–1952 on the old court site, Vasagatan 1.

vackert_rattvik_start.name: 'Beautiful Rättvik' project begins
vackert_rattvik_start.note: Ran 1994–2005 to bridge the barrier that the highway and railway created towards Siljan; the 'Vattenspel' fountain on the square opened in 2000.

dalhalla_invigd.name: Dalhalla officially opened
dalhalla_invigd.note: Test concert June 1993, first season concert 23 July 1994, official opening 21 June 1995 in a former limestone quarry; about 6,000 seats.

musik_vid_siljan_start.name: 'Musik vid Siljan' festival begins
musik_vid_siljan_start.note: Celebrated its 50th anniversary in 2019 and then ended; Stämmoveckan took over in 2021. The start year 1969 is our inference from the anniversary.

siljansringen_alder.name: Age of the Siljan Ring impact
siljansringen_alder.note: The culture house's nature museum says 377 million years (dates of 376.8 ± 1.7 and 377 ± 2 Ma). Other local sources say about 380.

siljansringen_diameter.name: Diameter of the Siljan Ring
siljansringen_diameter.note: Europe's largest known impact structure; Lake Siljan lies on its south-western rim.

prastskogsvallen_invigd.name: Prästskogsvallen sports ground opened
prastskogsvallen_invigd.note: Open-access sports ground with lit artificial turf, running track and a winter ice rink.

siljansoring_lekomraden_utestangda.name: Former spawning and nursery grounds of the Siljan trout shut off by hydropower development
siljansoring_lekomraden_utestangda.note: Building out the main channel of the Österdalälven in 1955–1970 shut the Siljan trout, the 'Siljan salmon', a large, long-migrating stock, out of more than 95% of its former spawning and nursery grounds (p. 9). The trout in Lake Siljan has fallen from thousands of individuals to a few hundred, and the eel has disappeared entirely; this is why Siljan has only moderate ecological status (p. 12). Trout have been stocked as compensation since the early 1950s.

osterdalalven_fiskvagar.name: Hydropower plants on the Österdalälven where fish passes for trout are being built
osterdalalven_fiskvagar.note: Following the 2019 settlement (M 7483-17), fish passes are being built past the power plants at Spjutmo, Blyberg and Väsa, so that the remaining spawning grounds in the river and its tributaries can be reached; the upstream pass at Spjutmo and the downstream passes at all three came into use in summer 2023. Trout stocking is now meant to help build a naturally reproducing stock rather than only compensate the fishery.

vindkraft_lokalagda_verk.name: Wind turbines on Hedbodberget owned by the municipality and its residents
vindkraft_lokalagda_verk.note: The municipality bought two of the first turbines on Hedbodberget (Vestas V90, 2 MW): one was sold as shares to residents in the association Rättviksvind, the other supplies the municipality and its companies. The wind farm's community fund goes to development in Dalfors and Orebygden. The association's current status was not found (research/deep/energi-resor).
