befolkning_siljansbygden_1990_2024.name: Population change 1990–2024 in Leksand, the neighbouring municipality by Lake Siljan that grew most
befolkning_siljansbygden_1990_2024.note: Population 1990 → 2024: Leksand 14,805 → 16,137 (+9.0%), Mora 20,549 → 20,540 (±0), Gagnef 10,453 → 10,384 (−0.7%), Rättvik 11,345 → 10,998 (−3.1%), Orsa 7,351 → 6,851 (−6.8%), Malung-Sälen 11,605 → 10,254 (−11.6%), Vansbro 7,901 → 6,752 (−14.5%), Älvdalen 8,353 → 6,882 (−17.6%). Åre, a rural municipality with tourism that turned decline into growth, went from 9,975 to 12,693 (+27.2%; +23.5% since 2010). Leksand grew most in the 1970s and 80s (12,347 inhabitants in 1970).

batlinje_rattvik_leksand_1895.name: The year the Gävle–Dala railway put a boat into service between Rättvik and Leksand
batlinje_rattvik_leksand_1895.note: Lake Siljan's first steamboat, Prins August, sailed from 1839. The first passenger boat, s/s Mora, ran from 1866 with one trip each way every weekday of the sailing season between Ål parish and Mora, and more piers were added as competition grew. The Gävle–Dala railway, which reached Rättvik in 1890, put a boat into service between Rättvik and Leksand in 1895 (S/S Rättvik, calling at Långbryggan). The service did well until the Siljan railway reached Rättvik in 1914; after that it ran excursions to Gesunda, Mora, Tunsta and Gråda. The boats came to be seen as slow once cars and the railway arrived, and the shipping companies' good years were over by the 1950s.

akermark_hektar.name: Arable land in Rättvik Municipality
akermark_hektar.note: Total arable land in the Swedish Board of Agriculture's area statistics (farm support applications and the farm register). The area has been almost unchanged since 2010 (2,365 ha) but was 2,666 ha in 1981 and 2,700 ha in 1985, i.e. 300–330 ha more than today.

vall_andel_akermark.name: Share of arable land under grass ley (hay and grazing)
vall_andel_akermark.note: 1,910 ha of ley in use divided by 2,368 ha of arable land in 2025. Including 135 ha of green fodder crops, just over 86% of the arable land grows feed for cattle, sheep and horses. In 1981 the ley share was 56% (1,480 of 2,666 ha).

spannmal_hektar.name: Cereal growing in Rättvik Municipality
spannmal_hektar.note: Total cereals in 2025: spring barley 136 ha, oats 62 ha, spring wheat 22 ha and winter wheat 8 ha etc., 9.7% of arable land; in addition 6 ha of table potatoes and 2 ha of horticultural crops. In 1981 at least 941 ha of cereals were grown, 756 ha of it barley (own sum of the crops), so the area has shrunk by more than three quarters.

betesmark_slatterang_hektar.name: Pasture and hay meadows in Rättvik Municipality
betesmark_slatterang_hektar.note: Total pasture and hay meadow in 2025: summer-farm (fäbod) grazing 608 ha, pasture 349 ha, hay meadow 6 ha and unspecified 9 ha. The area has varied between 766 and 1,825 ha since 2003, and the swings are mainly in fäbod grazing (449–1,322 ha).

fabodbete_hektar.name: Summer-farm (fäbod) grazing in Rättvik Municipality
fabodbete_hektar.note: Forest grazing at summer farms registered in the farm support system. It is 63% of the municipality's pasture (608 of 971 ha), 12% of Dalarna's fäbod grazing (5,224 ha) and 4% of Sweden's (15,703 ha). Rättvik ranks third in the county after Malung-Sälen (1,975 ha) and Älvdalen (1,351 ha).

fabodbete_foretag_lan.name: Farm businesses with summer-farm (fäbod) grazing in Dalarna
fabodbete_foretag_lan.note: Number of businesses with fäbod grazing in the county in 2025 (78 in 2023 and 2024); 205 in all of Sweden. The number is not published per municipality. In 2008 the County Administrative Board counted 85 actively used summer-farm sites with 100 farmers in Dalarna, of which only about twenty had traditional operation with milking and dairy processing (report 2008:12).

jordbruksforetag_antal.name: Farm businesses in Rättvik Municipality
jordbruksforetag_antal.note: All size groups; there were 106 in 2020. Farms with more than 2 ha of arable land have halved from 210 in 1981 to 103 in 2025 (own sum of the size groups). Eleven farms have more than 50 ha of arable land, and the County Administrative Board judges that seven are large enough to employ more than one person full time.

mjolkkor_antal.name: Dairy cows in Rättvik Municipality
mjolkkor_antal.note: Dairy cows in June 2023 on only five farms (twelve in 2010); there were 909 dairy cows in 1981. Even so, milk production covers the municipality's entire consumption, according to the County Administrative Board. Municipal figures exist for 2010, 2013, 2016, 2020 and 2023.

notkreatur_antal.name: Cattle in Rättvik Municipality
notkreatur_antal.note: Sum of dairy cows (437), suckler cows (255), heifers, bulls and steers (591) and calves under one year (410) in June 2023. The corresponding sum was 1,975 in 1981, 1,859 in 2010 and 1,613 in 2020. Suckler cows have grown from 10 in 1981 to 255 while dairy cows have halved; there were also 181 horses in 2023.

far_antal.name: Sheep (ewes and rams) in Rättvik Municipality
far_antal.note: Ewes and rams in June 2023 on 27 farms, plus 560 lambs. The number has almost doubled since 1981 (317) and 1990 (288); the 2019 comprehensive plan notes that sheep are often kept as a hobby.

sjalvforsorjningsgrad_vikt_lan.name: Food self-sufficiency in Dalarna, by weight
sjalvforsorjningsgrad_vikt_lan.note: The county's production (90,000 tonnes) divided by its consumption (239,000 tonnes), assuming everything produced stays in the county; Sweden as a whole is at 75%. The County Administrative Board stresses that the calculation is very uncertain; the previous situation report (2022) gave 42%. Only 10% of the raw materials cannot be produced locally, such as coffee, tea, rice and exotic fruit.

sjalvforsorjningsgrad_energi_lan.name: Food self-sufficiency in Dalarna, by energy
sjalvforsorjningsgrad_energi_lan.note: Production corresponds to 890 kcal per person per day against consumption of 3,000 kcal. The Swedish Food Agency's crisis diet is 2,450 kcal, so the county's primary production covers just over a third of crisis needs, and less if the raw materials must also be processed in the county.

sjalvforsorjningsgrad_notkott.name: Self-sufficiency in beef in Rättvik Municipality
sjalvforsorjningsgrad_notkott.note: The County Administrative Board's calculation of local production against local consumption. In the same calculation milk production covers the municipality's entire consumption, while the cereal harvest covers one fifth.

sjalvforsorjningsgrad_lamm.name: Self-sufficiency in lamb in Rättvik Municipality
sjalvforsorjningsgrad_lamm.note: Same calculation as for beef. Overall, primary production in the municipality is 'clearly lower than consumption', according to the County Administrative Board.

livsmedelskedjan_sysselsatta.name: People employed in the food chain in Rättvik Municipality
livsmedelskedjan_sysselsatta.note: The County Administrative Board's estimate, from farming to restaurants; half are women and most work in restaurants and retail. In all of Dalarna 9,500 people work in the food chain.

livsmedelsforadlare_antal.name: Food processing businesses in Rättvik Municipality
livsmedelsforadlare_antal.note: Sum of the County Administrative Board's list: Nya Siljans Chark (slaughterhouse, 25 employees), Rättviks glass (ice cream, 11 employees), five bakeries, two chocolate makers, one brewery and three other meat businesses. In addition there are five greenhouse businesses (two growing ornamentals), ten food shops and 47 restaurants.

akermark_per_invanare.name: Arable land per inhabitant in Rättvik Municipality
akermark_per_invanare.note: 2,343 ha of arable land divided by 11,042 inhabitants in 2023, just above the world average of 0.19 ha. With Swedish consumption and average world yields, at least 0.38 ha per person would be needed for self-sufficiency, according to the County Administrative Board.

skogsmark_andel_landareal.name: Forest land as share of land area
skogsmark_andel_landareal.note: 172,707 ha of forest land (157,660 ha of it productive) divided by 193,047 ha of land in 2020. Open mire takes another 5.9% (11,463 ha). Water covers 21,942 ha, 10% of the municipality's total area.

jordbruksmark_andel_landareal.name: Agricultural land as share of land area
jordbruksmark_andel_landareal.note: 3,260 ha of agricultural land (2,347 ha arable and 913 ha pasture) divided by 193,047 ha of land in 2020; in 2010 it was 3,513 ha. The 2019 comprehensive plan says 'just under three per cent' and describes the land as small-scale, lime-rich and fertile, mainly along the lakes of the Siljan Ring.

bebyggd_mark_andel_landareal.name: Built-up and developed land as share of land area
bebyggd_mark_andel_landareal.note: 4,462 ha of built-up and developed land (buildings, plots, roads, railway etc.) divided by 193,047 ha of land in 2020. In 2010 the area was 4,309 ha, so it grew by 153 ha in ten years, about 15 ha a year.

skog_privatpersoner_andel.name: Share of productive forest land owned by private individuals
skog_privatpersoner_andel.note: 51,000 ha of declared productive forest land owned by natural persons divided by 157,000 ha in total in 2025; both figures are rounded to thousands of hectares. The rest is owned by companies, the state and other public or private owners. Of the private individuals' forest, 31,000 ha is owned by residents of the municipality and 14,000 ha by owners living outside Dalarna.

skogsagare_privatpersoner_antal.name: Private individuals owning forest in Rättvik Municipality
skogsagare_privatpersoner_antal.note: 1,235 of the owners are registered residents of the municipality, 377 live elsewhere in Dalarna and 679 outside the county; 952 are women. The number has fallen from 2,740 in 1999. The median holding per management unit is only 11 ha while the mean is 85 ha (table PX12).

foryngringsavverkning_anmald_hektar.name: Notified regeneration felling (clear-cutting) in Rättvik Municipality
foryngringsavverkning_anmald_hektar.note: Felling notifications and permit applications in 2025: 708 ha by private owners and 708 ha by other owners. The 2021–2025 average was 1,405 ha a year (0.9% of the productive forest land), against 2,030 ha a year in 2010–2014, when other owners notified far more. Notified area is not the same as area actually felled.

naturreservat_antal.name: Nature reserves in Rättvik Municipality
naturreservat_antal.note: 29 nature reserves in force covering 3,724 ha in total (3,611 ha of land), ten of them created since 2015. The newest is the municipal Lerdalsberget reserve next to Rättvik's ski slope, decided by the municipal council on 7 May 2026 (13.9 ha in the register, about 12 ha according to the decision). The municipality's own web page still counts 27.

natura2000_omraden_antal.name: Natura 2000 sites in Rättvik Municipality
natura2000_omraden_antal.note: 14 sites lie entirely within the municipality (1,688 ha), and the Voxnan river (912 ha) is shared with Ovanåker and Ljusdal. Gåsberget and Glistjärn are designated under both the Habitats and the Birds Directive; Glistjärn, near the lime works north of the town, is described as the municipality's finest bird lake.

rodlistade_arter_observerade_antal.name: Red-listed species recorded in Rättvik Municipality since 2000
rodlistade_arter_observerade_antal.note: Number of distinct species on the 2020 Swedish Red List with at least one record from 2000–2026 in the municipality, extracted on 11 October 2026 (729 species for all years, 511 since 2010). The figure reflects both species richness and survey effort; protected records have generalised coordinates and the 2025 Red List was not yet in the database. The most recorded species are the marsh fritillary butterfly, the lichen Alectoria sarmentosa and the orchid creeping lady's-tresses.

geosites_antal.name: Geosites of Siljan Geopark within Rättvik Municipality
geosites_antal.note: The municipality lists twelve geosites: the Amtjärn quarry, Boda church, Dalhalla, the Enån nature reserve, Fjäckan, Långbryggan, the Solberga limestone quarry, Springkällan, Styggforsen, Vidablick, Vindförbergs udde and the Östbjörka nature reserve. Siljan Geopark is run by Leksand, Mora, Orsa and Rättvik with the County Administrative Board and Visit Dalarna; it became Sweden's first national geopark in 2019, and SGU extended the status by five years in November 2025. The meteorite impact that created the Siljan Ring has been dated to 377 million years ago (SGU report 2010:21).

gronyta_andel_tatort.name: Green space in Rättvik town, share of land area
gronyta_andel_tatort.note: 854 ha of green space (490 ha open land and 364 ha forest) divided by 1,242 ha of land in the built-up area in 2020; there is also 114 ha of arable land. Publicly accessible green space is 499 ha (40%). Statistics Sweden counts private gardens and lawns between houses as green space.

hardgjord_mark_andel_tatort.name: Sealed (impervious) land in Rättvik town, share of land area
hardgjord_mark_andel_tatort.note: 272 ha of sealed land divided by 1,242 ha of land in 2020: buildings 78 ha, roads and railway 103 ha and other sealed surfaces 91 ha. In 2015 the share was 22.1% (274 of 1,238 ha).

tradbevuxen_mark_andel_tatort.name: Forest-covered land in Rättvik town, share of land area
tradbevuxen_mark_andel_tatort.note: 364 ha of land classed as forest within the town's green space divided by 1,242 ha of land in 2020 (388 ha and 31.3% in 2015). It is not a tree-canopy measurement: street trees and scattered garden trees are not counted, so it may underestimate canopy cover. No canopy-cover figure for Rättvik has been found.

narhet_gronomrade_200m_andel.name: Share of town residents with a green area within 200 metres
narhet_gronomrade_200m_andel.note: Covers the 5,318 residents of Rättvik town and green areas of at least 0.5 ha; 98% have one within 300 m and 100% within 500 m. The town has 167 such green areas totalling 345 ha, four of them larger than 10 ha.

lis_omraden_antal.name: Lakeshore rural-development (LIS) areas in the comprehensive plan
lis_omraden_antal.note: Of 24 shoreline areas studied, 20 were designated where exemptions from shoreline protection can be granted on rural-development grounds; five are on Lake Siljan (Ickviken–Vikarbyn, Stumsnäs, Tina–Gärdebyn, the boat harbour and Lerdal). Shoreline protection is otherwise 100 m, extended at Säsvik on Oresjön and at Sollen and Storholmen in Amungen (plan part 2). The 2024 planning strategy judges that the LIS plan needs revision.

detaljplanerad_mark_smahus_antal.name: Land zoned for detached houses (planning reserve)
detaljplanerad_mark_smahus_antal.note: The comprehensive plan states that zoned land exists for 'just over 250 detached houses', mainly in central Rättvik, Lerdal–Gärdebyn, Vikarbyn and Furudal, but several plans are old and lack roads or water and sewerage. At the time 5–10 houses were being built a year, and the town lacks flats in apartment buildings.

detaljplaner_pagaende_antal.name: Detailed development plans in active preparation in Rättvik Municipality
detaljplaner_pagaende_antal.note: Active plans: Klockargården (detached houses), Utsikten, Persborg and Siljansborg (housing, Siljansborg also temporary accommodation), Haga- and Börjes väg (streets, nature and stormwater), Stora Lissbrändan, and Garvaren, Mangeln and Färgaren. Utsikten (about 47 house plots south of the ski slope) was adopted by the municipal council on 11 June 2026, and the development agreement for Klockargården (up to seven plots) was approved on 7 May 2026. Nine assignments are queued, among them a new comprehensive plan with an in-depth plan for Rättvik–Vikarbyn, 'Vackert Rättvik 2.0' and the Hedslund sports ground.

persborg_planerade_bostader.name: Planned homes in the new Persborg area
persborg_planerade_bostader.note: About 100 homes in apartment buildings, detached and semi-detached houses, conceived as multigenerational housing in an eco-village; the detailed plan is prioritised but the design is not settled. Students at Dalarna University produced nine proposals in spring 2026. The site is in Sjurberg on Lake Siljan, where the tourist hotel Persborg stood; a 1960s–70s cabin village now occupies the hotel site (heritage programme 2026).

langbryggan_kajreparation_kostnad.name: Cost of repairing Långbryggan's outer quay in 2020
langbryggan_kajreparation_kostnad.note: The municipality's cost of 'around half a million kronor' after a storm in January 2020 tore up the planks where the Gustaf Wasa docks; according to Dala-Demokraten the job grew larger than expected and the whole quay was rebuilt with a new wave guard. The pier is 628 m long, was built in 1895 and reopened on 6 June 1992 after a major renovation partly financed by 2,938 named planks; that was the last major repair before 2020.

lokstallarna_renovering_kostnad.name: Renovation cost of Lokstallarna (engine sheds) at Rättvik station
lokstallarna_renovering_kostnad.note: Estimated total cost of the multi-year renovation of the engine shed from about 1890, which the municipality took over in 2006. The building reopened on 4 June 2025 with four halls totalling 800 m² and up to 15 m ceiling height for culture, food, crafts and associations (municipal news item, 4 June 2025).

byggnadsminnen_antal.name: Listed buildings (byggnadsminnen) in Rättvik Municipality
byggnadsminnen_antal.note: Among them the 1840s spa pavilion at Hvilan in Lerdal (listed 1988), Solgården (1897) and Tånggården in Sjurberg, Danielsgården in Bingsjö, Matsgården in Östbjörka and the Blånnes barn in Gärdsjö; the 2019 comprehensive plan counted ten. Rättvik church is instead protected as an ecclesiastical monument, and according to the Diocese of Västerås's assessment (2006) the adjoining church stables are also covered by the heritage law.

riksintressen_kulturmiljo_antal.name: Areas of national interest for cultural heritage in Rättvik Municipality
riksintressen_kulturmiljo_antal.note: There are also 55 municipal heritage areas, and a heritage programme was adopted by the municipal executive board on 17 March 2026. Closest to the centre is Kyrkudden (W 89) with the medieval church, a tithe barn from 1758 and 87 church stables, one of them tree-ring dated to 1492 according to the heritage programme. Five of the national-interest areas are summer-farm environments (Swedish National Heritage Board's list).

kretsloppsplan_mal_avfallsminskning.name: Target in the 2023–2030 waste plan: less waste generated by 2030
kretsloppsplan_mal_avfallsminskning.note: The waste plan for Rättvik, Leksand, Gagnef and Vansbro was adopted in Rättvik on 22 February 2024: waste is to fall by at least 25% and waste sent to incineration by 50% by 2030. Households take bulky waste to the Drafsån recycling centre (open around the clock with 'Anytime') and to Furudal, and since October 2025 the municipality's Ta Till Vara shop at Riksvägen 23 sells reused goods collected from a staffed container at Drafsån.

befolkning_1970.name: Population in 1970
befolkning_1970.note: Population on 31 December within today's municipal boundary (SCB reports 1968–1982 on the 1983 division; Rättvik Municipality was formed in 1971 and Ore was added in 1974). In 1968 the area had 11,300 inhabitants; the 1970s low was 10,634 (1973).

befolkning_1990.name: Population in 1990
befolkning_1990.note: The population grew during the 1980s and peaked at 11,418 in 1992. It then fell to a low of 10,748 in 2014.

befolkning_2010.name: Population in 2010
befolkning_2010.note: The population has stayed between 10,600 and 11,450 since 1970. After 2014 it rose to 11,103 in 2021 (high in-migration during the pandemic years); it was 10,978 on 31 December 2025 and 10,962 in August 2026 (SCB, BE0101).

befolkning_prognos_2030.name: Population in 2030 according to SCB's regional projection (2024)
befolkning_prognos_2030.note: The projection starts from 11,053 inhabitants in 2024 and 11,061 in 2025. The outcome was 10,978 (December 2025) and 10,962 (August 2026), i.e. below SCB's path. The municipality's own forecast in its 2025 annual report gives 10,965 in 2034, against SCB's 11,103.

befolkning_prognos_2040.name: Population in 2040 according to SCB's regional projection (2024)
befolkning_prognos_2040.note: SCB's projection (published 11 June 2024) gives an almost unchanged population: 11,106 in 2035 and 11,107 in 2040. It assumes a natural decrease of about 100 a year offset by in-migration; the number of people aged 20–64 falls from 5,326 (2024) to about 5,250 (2030–2040).

befolkning_prognos_2070.name: Population in 2070 according to SCB's regional projection (2024)
befolkning_prognos_2070.note: SCB's longest projection for the municipality: 11,224 in 2050, 11,393 in 2060 and 11,580 in 2070. On average it assumes 79 births and 180 deaths a year in 2025–2070 (own calculation from the table), which requires net in-migration of just over 100 a year. No official projection beyond 2070 exists.

andel_65plus_prognos_2040.name: Share of residents aged 65 and over in 2040 according to SCB's projection
andel_65plus_prognos_2040.note: 4,054 of 11,107 residents are 65+ in 2040 (summed over single-year ages in SCB's table). Projection base year 2024: 34.3%; 2070: 37.4%. Dalarna County in 2040: 28.9%.

andel_80plus_prognos_2040.name: Share of residents aged 80 and over in 2040 according to SCB's projection
andel_80plus_prognos_2040.note: 1,605 of 11,107 residents are 80+ in 2040, against 10.7% in 2024 and 16.4% in 2070; the fastest rise comes before 2030 (already 14.0% then). The 2025 outcome was 1,236 people or 11.3% (annual report 2025). Dalarna County in 2040: 10.8%.

fodelseoverskott_2025.name: Natural increase (births minus deaths)
fodelseoverskott_2025.note: 72 births and 143 deaths in 2025, that is 6.6 and 13.0 per 1,000 residents (own calculation; Sweden 9.2 and 8.7). Deaths have exceeded births every year since at least 2000; 2015–2024 averaged 79 births and 159 deaths a year. First half of 2026: 30 births and 90 deaths.

flyttnetto_2025.name: Net migration (domestic and international)
flyttnetto_2025.note: 535 in-movers and 479 out-movers: net −30 against the rest of Dalarna and +57 against the rest of Sweden, and net immigration +28 (48 immigrants, 20 emigrants). 2015–2024 averaged +101 a year (own calculation), with peaks in 2016 (+203, refugee reception) and 2020 (+168). First half of 2026: +53.

fritidshus_antal.name: Second homes owned by private persons or estates
fritidshus_antal.note: Up from 2,520 in 1998 (+18%). That is 271 second homes per 1,000 residents, against 164 in Dalarna County and 60 in Sweden (own calculation with SCB's 2025 population). Company-owned second homes are not included.

sommarbefolkning_topp_faktor.name: Summer population peak (Saturday of Classic Car Week) relative to the annual median
sommarbefolkning_topp_faktor.note: SCB's analysis of mobile-network data (Telia Crowd Insights) for summer 2023: "On the Saturday of Classic Car Week the population of Rättvik triples". For most of the summer the population was close to the annual median; Rättvik belongs to the municipalities with a few peak days rather than a long summer season. No absolute count of summer residents exists.

ensamhet_besvar.name: Share of residents 16+ bothered by loneliness sometimes, often or always
ensamhet_besvar.note: Health on Equal Terms 2024 with Dalarna's extra sample (about 940 respondents in Rättvik). Confidence interval 10.2–14.5%, significantly below Sweden (18.2%); Dalarna 17.2%. The question is only reported for 2024, so there is no time series.

ensamhet_ofta.name: Share of residents 16+ bothered by loneliness often or always
ensamhet_ofta.note: Confidence interval 2.7–5.1%, significantly below Sweden (5.5%); Dalarna 5.4%.

lagt_socialt_deltagande.name: Share of residents with low social participation (latest pre-pandemic measurement)
lagt_socialt_deltagande.note: The indicator counts how few of the survey's social activities a person took part in during the past year. 2014: Rättvik 26.5% (CI 23.7–29.4), Dalarna 25.4%, Sweden 20.4%. The 2021 survey gave 61.1% (Dalarna 53.7%, Sweden 48.6%) but was taken under pandemic restrictions and is not comparable; the question is not reported for 2024.

positiv_syn_pa_framtiden.name: Share of residents 16+ who always or mostly feel positive about the future
positiv_syn_pa_framtiden.note: The survey's closest measure of hope and sense of meaning. CI 70.3–76.0%; Dalarna 71.3%, Sweden 72.0%. In 2021 the share was 80.7% in Rättvik, a fall of 7.5 percentage points in three years (Dalarna −5.2).

radd_ga_ut_ensam.name: Share of residents 16+ who have refrained from going out alone for fear of being attacked
radd_ga_ut_ensam.note: CI 10.6–14.9%, significantly below Sweden (28.3%); Dalarna 22.9%. In 2014 the share was 8.8% in Rättvik. Kolada U01420 (years 2021–2024 pooled) gives 13.2%.

ensamhet_hemtjanst_65plus.name: Share of people aged 65+ with home care who are bothered by loneliness
ensamhet_hemtjanst_65plus.note: Share answering 'yes, mild' or 'yes, severe' in the National Board of Health and Welfare's survey of people 65+ receiving home care; Sweden 51.0%. Severe: 8.7% (Sweden 10.0%, Kolada U21478). Compare 3.9% of all residents 16+ who are often or always bothered by loneliness.

klarar_inte_ovantad_utgift.name: Share of residents 16+ who could not cover an unexpected expense
klarar_inte_ovantad_utgift.note: CI 17.2–22.3%; Dalarna 21.4%, Sweden 20.3%; in 2021 the share was 20.5% in Rättvik. According to Kolada (Health on Equal Terms 2021–2024 pooled) 14.5% have had an economic crisis in the past year (U01407) and 11.3% have gone without dental care for financial reasons (N01464, Sweden 10.5%).

unga_nojda_med_livet.name: Share of young people (lower and upper secondary) who are very or fairly satisfied with life as a whole
unga_nojda_med_livet.note: 158 of 179 respondents (Dalarna 86%); upper secondary 91%, lower secondary 86%, and 81% in 2021. The picture differs from the school-health interviews, where 66.7% of first-year upper-secondary students say they feel good; the questions and samples differ.

unga_tror_flytta_fran_kommunen.name: Share of young people (lower and upper secondary) who think they will move away from the municipality
unga_tror_flytta_fran_kommunen.note: 114 of 180 respondents in Rättvik (Dalarna 56%; Rättvik 2021: 66%), among upper-secondary students 78% (Dalarna 73%). Of those who expect to move, 54% give work and 37% further studies as the reason. The best things about living in the municipality: family and relatives (53%) and nearness to nature (38%).

gymnasieelever_ar1_mar_bra.name: Share of first-year upper-secondary students who feel good or very good most of the time
gymnasieelever_ar1_mar_bra.note: (26 'very good' + 64 'good') / 135 respondents in the school-health interviews at the municipality's upper-secondary school, which also has students from other municipalities; Dalarna 75.4%, and Rättvik 67.8% in school year 2024/25. 42% of the students felt low or sad at least once a week (Dalarna 30%). In year 7, 85% felt good (Dalarna 80%).

unga_mojlighet_paverka.name: Share of young people who feel they have good opportunities to put their views to the municipality's decision-makers
unga_mojlighet_paverka.note: 39 of 180 respondents in lower and upper secondary answer very or fairly good opportunities (Dalarna 16%). 36% have very or fairly high trust in politicians (Dalarna 38%), against 45% in 2021.

valdeltagande_kommunval_2022.name: Turnout in the 2022 municipal council election
valdeltagande_kommunval_2022.note: 7,813 of 9,289 eligible voters; lowest voting district 75.3%, highest 88.0% (Vikarbyn) according to Kolada N05831/N05833. The election of 13 September 2026 gave exactly the same turnout, 84.11% (7,780 of 9,250; Dalarna County 83.33%, Sweden 82.34%). Seats 2022: S 11, C 10, M 7, SD 7, KD 3, V 1; 2026: S 13, C 8, M 8, SD 7, KD 2, V 1.

barnfattigdom_andel.name: Share of children aged 0–17 in economic hardship (Save the Children's revised measure)
barnfattigdom_andel.note: 161 of 1,714 children live in households with a low income standard based on the Consumer Agency's basic needs and/or receiving social assistance; rank 75 of 290 municipalities. Dalarna County 14.3%, Sweden 12.9%; with Save the Children's earlier measure 5.7% (98 children). The same figures are in the report's Excel annex for counties and municipalities 2023.

skattesats_total_2026.name: Total municipal tax rate 2026 (municipality + region)
skattesats_total_2026.note: 21.81% to the municipality and 11.99% to Region Dalarna. The national average is 32.38% and Dalarna County's 34.18%. Unchanged since 2025; 33.45% in 2020.

sarskilt_boende_65plus_antal.name: People aged 65+ in special housing (residential care)
sarskilt_boende_65plus_antal.note: Median over the year, including needs-assessed sheltered housing; 148 in 2021. That is 3.05% of residents aged 65+ (Sweden 3.82%, Kolada N23890). The municipality rents 185 flats from Rättviks Fastigheter for elderly and disability housing, and its housing plan for older people is being revised (annual report 2025).

hemtjanst_65plus_antal.name: People aged 65+ receiving home care in ordinary housing
hemtjanst_65plus_antal.note: Up from 250 (2022) and 270 (2024); 224 of them are 80+. In all, 25.6% of residents aged 80+ have home care or special housing (Sweden 25.5%, Kolada N20892), against 33.5% in 2018: more older people are cared for at home and fewer live in care homes.

listade_invanare_per_allmanlakare.name: Listed residents per full-time GP (specialist in general practice) at health centres
listade_invanare_per_allmanlakare.note: The National Board of Health and Welfare's guideline is 1,100; the survey average for Sweden is 1,750 and regions range from 1,275 to 2,337. 66% of the county's 29 health centres responded; Rättvik health centre (Region Dalarna, in the same building as the Prästskogen care home) is not reported separately.

hyrlakare_andel_vardcentral.name: Share of GP specialist work at health centres done by agency (locum) doctors
hyrlakare_andel_vardcentral.note: In Region Dalarna 80% of the work is done by permanent staff and 2% by substitutes. Sweden 11%; highest in Gävleborg (31%) and lowest in Halland (0%). The report warns that long-term dependence on agency doctors puts continuity of care at risk.

gymnasieelever_i_kommunen.name: Students at upper-secondary schools located in the municipality (Stiernhööksgymnasiet)
gymnasieelever_i_kommunen.note: Counted on 15 October 2025; the largest programme is natural resource use (the national upper-secondary school for naturbruk) with about 190 students, followed by electricity and energy (about 60), building, business and social science (about 50 each), introductory programmes (about 40) and natural science (about 10), according to the Swedish National Agency for Education 2025/26. The agriculture track had 42 first-choice applicants for 24 places in 2025. Of the 308 upper-secondary students registered in Rättvik, 28% attend another municipality's school (Sweden 20%).

bostader_antal.name: Number of dwellings (all building types including special housing)
bostader_antal.note: Sum of the table cells: 3,753 in one- or two-dwelling houses (64%), 1,680 in multi-dwelling buildings, 137 in other buildings and 292 special-housing units. Up 270 since 2015 (5,592), about 27 a year. In addition there are 2,980 second homes.

andel_hyresratt.name: Share of dwellings that are rental flats (including special housing)
andel_hyresratt.note: 1,590 of 5,862 dwellings. Owner-occupied houses 3,574 (61.0%), tenant-owned (bostadsrätt) 694 (11.8%). Excluding special housing the rental share is 23.3% (1,298 of 5,570).

allmannyttan_lagenheter.name: Flats owned by the municipal housing company Rättviks Fastigheter AB
allmannyttan_lagenheter.note: About 36,000 m² of residential floor area; in addition the municipality block-rents 185 flats for elderly and disability housing, and the page 'Våra bostadsområden' (2025) gives 594 flats in three categories: ordinary (from age 18), 55+ and sheltered housing (from age 70). The queue has grown (annual report 2025), but its length is not published. The company plans two buildings with eight flats in Boda, ready in spring 2027.

kollektivhus_lagenheter_lan.name: Flats in cohousing communities in Dalarna County (members of Kollektivhus NU)
kollektivhus_lagenheter_lan.note: The only house in the county is Tersen in Falun: a cooperative rental for 'the second half of life' with 44 flats. There is no start-up group in Dalarna and no cohousing in Rättvik. Houses that are not members of the association are not on the list.

foreningar_i_registret.name: Associations in the municipality's register of associations
foreningar_i_registret.note: Sum of the register's categories: 33 sports clubs, 24 village-hall associations, 13 other, 9 cultural associations (incl. the Rättvik, Boda and Ore local-history societies and Boda fiddlers' group), 6 adult-education associations, 3 pensioners' associations, 2 church, 2 political and 1 disability association. Only associations that chose to be listed are included.

unga_medlem_forening.name: Share of young people (lower and upper secondary) who are members of an association
unga_medlem_forening.note: 95 of 180 respondents (Dalarna 50%). Lower secondary 62% (Dalarna 55%), upper secondary 45% (Dalarna 43%). 62% think there is a lot or quite a lot to do in their free time (Dalarna 63%).

idrottsforeningar_lok_per_10000.name: Sports clubs receiving state LOK activity grants per 10,000 residents
idrottsforeningar_lok_per_10000.note: About 19 clubs (own calculation: 17.28 × 1.0998). Sweden 9.59. Participation is lower, however: 25.7 activity sessions per resident aged 7–20 against 33.4 in Sweden (Kolada U09800).

anmalda_brott_per_100000.name: Reported crimes per 100,000 residents
anmalda_brott_per_100000.note: Sweden 13,581. The rise from 7,305 (2024) is large; the cause has not been checked in BRÅ's statistics by offence type, and in a small municipality single cases with many reports can make a big difference. Reported violent crimes 2025: 1,110 per 100,000 (Sweden 1,067).

utsatthet_brott_mot_person_ntu.name: Share of people aged 16–84 exposed to crime against the person (Swedish Crime Survey, NTU)
utsatthet_brott_mot_person_ntu.note: At least one of: card or sales fraud, pickpocketing, robbery, sexual offence, assault, threats, harassment or online abuse in the previous year; Sweden 20.0%. For Rättvik only 2020–2021 exists (10.5%, two years pooled). Worry about crime in society: Dalarna 52.2% (2025), Sweden 53.6%.

gastnatter.name: Guest nights in commercial accommodation
gastnatter.note: All guest nights in 2025 at hotels, campsites, cabin villages, hostels and agency-let cottages that report to the accommodation statistics, +0.6% on 2024 (Swedish 201,559, foreign 24,788). Stays in own second homes, with relatives or via Airbnb are not included. In the portal choose level Kommun, municipality Rättvik and period 2025-01 to 2025-12.

gastnatter_2019.name: Guest nights in commercial accommodation 2019 (pre-pandemic)
gastnatter_2019.note: The peak pre-pandemic year, +7.7% on 2018 (Swedish 253,421, foreign 26,014); hotels 23%, camping 38%, hostels 6% and confidential accommodation types 34%. In 2025 Rättvik was 19% below 2019, while the four Siljan municipalities together were 9% below.

gastnatter_2020.name: Guest nights in commercial accommodation 2020 (pandemic year)
gastnatter_2020.note: −27.6% on 2019. Foreign guest nights fell 69% to 7,970 and Swedish ones 23% to 194,943.

gastnatter_2023.name: Guest nights in commercial accommodation 2023
gastnatter_2023.note: −12.0% on 2022, when 263,802 guest nights marked a peak during the post-pandemic staycation boom. Foreign guest nights 22,204.

gastnatter_2024.name: Guest nights in commercial accommodation 2024
gastnatter_2024.note: −2.9% on 2023: Swedish guest nights fell 5.1% while foreign ones rose 17.3% to 26,051. Camping 52%, hotels 23%.

gastnatter_sommar_andel.name: Share of the year's guest nights in June–August
gastnatter_sommar_andel.note: 149,979 guest nights in June–August 2025 divided by 226,773 for the whole year = 66.1%; July alone had 80,487 (35%), 74% of them on campsites. In 2019 the share was 63.4% (178,305 / 281,099): since then summer has fallen 16% and the rest of the year 25%.

gastnatter_vinter.name: Guest nights in the winter season December–March
gastnatter_vinter.note: December 2024–March 2025, −9.7% on the previous winter (28,965); about 12% of the 2025 annual total (own comparison, periods do not fully overlap). For Dalarna as a whole roughly half of all guest nights fall in winter (3.07 million December 2025–April 2026 according to Visit Dalarna), mainly in the mountains.

utlandska_gastnatter_andel.name: Foreign guests' share of guest nights
utlandska_gastnatter_andel.note: 24,788 foreign guest nights out of 226,773 in 2025 (−4.8% on 2024); largest markets Norway, Germany, the Netherlands, the UK and Denmark. The share was 9.3% in 2019 and 11.6% in 2024, against 15.4% in the four Siljan municipalities and 20% in Dalarna.

camping_andel_gastnatter.name: Camping's share of guest nights
camping_andel_gastnatter.note: Camping 52.6%, hotels 23.0% and confidential accommodation types (cabin villages, hostels, agency-let cottages) 24.4% of guest nights in 2025. Camping's share was 37.7% in 2019; campers are weather-sensitive and concentrated in July.

gastnatter_per_invanare.name: Guest nights per inhabitant
gastnatter_per_invanare.note: The year's commercial guest nights divided by the population on 31 December. Dalarna 18.0 and Sweden 6.7; Leksand 21.8, Orsa 19.6 and Mora 16.4 (2025); Rättvik had 25.7 in 2019.

disponibla_baddar.name: Available beds per day in commercial accommodation (annual average)
disponibla_baddar.note: On average 1,020 beds per day in 2025 (+1.8%), of which 244 occupied, giving an occupancy rate of 23.9%; for rooms 396 available and 34.1% occupancy. Campsite pitches for tents, caravans and motorhomes are probably not counted, so summer capacity is larger than this figure.

logiintakter.name: Accommodation revenue in commercial accommodation
logiintakter.note: SEK 79,886,431 in 2025, +1.5% on 2024, about SEK 350 per guest night (own calculation). The average rate per occupied room was SEK 1,092 and revenue per available room SEK 372; Dalarna county had SEK 2,005 million (Tillväxtverket, Inkvartering 2025, p. 13).

gastnatter_siljan.name: Guest nights in the four Siljan municipalities (Leksand, Mora, Orsa, Rättvik)
gastnatter_siljan.note: −1.4% on 2024 and 9% below 2019 (1,151,570); Rättvik's share is 21.6%. Leksand had about 352,400, Mora 335,500 and Orsa 135,100 (derived by stepwise selection in the portal, consistent with Kolada).

turismkonsumtion.name: Tourism consumption in the municipality (visitor spending)
turismkonsumtion.note: Spending by Swedish and foreign visitors in 2025: accommodation 29%, retail 23%, second homes/apartments 16%, culture 11%, restaurants 9%; about SEK 81,000 per inhabitant against the national SEK 47,500. In 2019 it was SEK 915 million in 2025 prices (−3%), and the four Siljan municipalities together had SEK 3,956 million in 2025. Experimental statistics that Tillväxtverket says should be read with caution at municipal level.

turism_arsarbetskrafter.name: Employment generated by tourism (full-time equivalents)
turism_arsarbetskrafter.note: Full-time jobs generated by visitor demand in the municipality in 2025, −2 on 2024 and 202 in 2019; seasonal jobs are converted to full-year, so more people work in the industry. The four Siljan municipalities together have 955. Experimental municipal statistics.

turism_andel_bkp.name: Tourism's share of the municipal economy (gross municipal product)
turism_andel_bkp.note: Share at current prices including taxes on products, 2023 is the latest year; tourism value added was SEK 182 million (44.9% in accommodation, 22.0% in retail, 18.6% in restaurants) and the municipality's GRP SEK 3,605 million. In 2019 the share was 8%, and in 2020 it fell to about 5.5%. Sweden 2.6%; neighbouring Orsa is among the ten municipalities in the country with the highest share.

overnattningar_eget_fritidshus_dalarna.name: Overnight stays in own second homes in Dalarna
overnattningar_eget_fritidshus_dalarna.note: Visit Dalarna's tourism economic model (TEM) gives 17.4 million tourist overnight stays in Dalarna in 2025, of which 7.6 million (44%; 4.6 million in 2019) in own second homes, more than the 5.15 million commercial guest nights. With the county's 46,945 second homes that is about 160 nights per second home per year (own calculation); TEM also gives SEK 12.6 billion in turnover and 7,795 FTEs in the county's visitor industry.

fritidshus.name: Second homes in the municipality
fritidshus.note: Small houses with no registered residents, owned by private persons or estates, per the property tax register on 1 January 2025; 2,520 in 1998 and 2,902 in 2019 (SCB table TAB825). That is 271 second homes per 1,000 inhabitants (Sweden 60); Leksand has 4,157, Mora 5,003 and Orsa 1,830.

fritidshus_lokalt_agda_andel.name: Share of second homes owned by people registered in the municipality
fritidshus_lokalt_agda_andel.note: So more than four in five second homes (about 83%) are owned by people in other municipalities, people abroad or estates, and the owners come from 160 municipalities. Nationally one in four second homes is locally owned.

befolkning_juli_okning.name: Increase in people present in July compared with October–November
befolkning_juli_okning.note: SCB experimental statistics from mobile network data (Telia, calibrated to population statistics): about 11,140 people in October–November, 17,630 in July (+6,490) and 20,310 at Midsummer (+82%) in 2022. Leksand rose 49% in July, Orsa 35% and Mora 22%.

befolkning_max_faktor.name: Peak summer presence relative to the year's median population (Classic Car Week Saturday)
befolkning_max_faktor.note: On Saturday 29 July 2023 at 20:00, mobile data showed three times as many people in the municipality as the year's median (about 10,000), the fifth-highest value among Swedish municipalities that summer. Leksand reached 2.4 times on Midsummer Eve.

classic_car_week_gastnatter.name: Guest nights linked to Classic Car Week (weeks 30–31)
classic_car_week_gastnatter.note: The municipality's situation report gives about 35,000 guest nights linked to the car week, plus day visitors; the figure probably also covers private letting, temporary camping and second homes. The organiser speaks of 10,000 cars during the week, held in week 31 since 1992; a 2018 parliamentary motion gave 40,000 guest nights.

classic_car_week_andel_brott.name: Share of the municipality's annual reported crimes reported during Classic Car Week
classic_car_week_andel_brott.note: Police assessment after the 2026 car week, when among other things five suspected rapes, 30 assaults and about 900 fineable offences were reported; 245 people were fined for loud music (89 in 2025). The municipality's situation report shows about 100 reported crimes in week 31 against about 20 in a normal week.

dalhalla_besokare.name: Concert visitors at Dalhalla per season
dalhalla_besokare.note: About 120,000 visitors in summer 2026 with the venue's highest average audience so far; the record is 129,000 (2023) and in 2012 it was 40,000 (dalhalla.se/historia). The Draggängarna limestone quarry, worked until 1990, became a concert venue in 1994–1995 and now holds about 4,800–6,000 people; up to 400 people are on the payroll each season.

rattviks_marknad_besokare.name: Visitors per Rättvik market (May and October)
rattviks_marknad_besokare.note: The municipality gives over 1,000 booked stalls and 100,000–120,000 visitors per market; the lower bound is used here. The market is held in early May and early October and dates back to the 1890s; an estimate, not a count.

skiddagar_2100_rcp45.name: Days per year with good skiing snow in southern Dalarna 2069–2098 (RCP4.5)
skiddagar_2100_rcp45.note: SMHI's calculation for Runn near Falun, the nearest example area (snow cover above 20 mm water equivalent): from about 90 days in 1961–1990 to just under 40 at the end of the century with limited emissions, and with high emissions (RCP8.5) good skiing becomes rare. There is no calculation for Rättvik, which lies somewhat further north.

vegetationsperiod_2100_rcp85.name: Length of the growing season around Siljan 2069–2098 (RCP8.5)
vegetationsperiod_2100_rcp85.note: The period with daily mean temperature above about 5 °C, on average 5 months around Siljan in 1961–1990, is projected to be about 7 months by the end of the century with high emissions (2–3 weeks shorter with RCP4.5). A longer summer half-year may favour camping and outdoor life, but SMHI also expects heatwaves of up to two weeks around Siljan.

klimat_hotellnatt.name: Climate impact per hotel night in Sweden
klimat_hotellnatt.note: Energy for heating, electricity, hot water and laundry at a four-star hotel (hostels and similar 0.9 kg); food and construction are excluded. Accommodation weighs little against the journey: a week in a hotel gives 26 kg, while 1,000 km by fossil car gives 76 kg per person.

klimat_bilresa_100mil.name: Climate impact per person of a 1,000 km holiday trip by fossil car (three people in the car)
klimat_bilresa_100mil.note: Mid-size diesel car, 229 g CO2e per vehicle-km including manufacture of the car, split between three travellers; the same distance by electric car in the Nordics gives 20 kg, bus 30 kg and Nordic train 7 kg per person. A week in a hotel gives 26 kg, so the journey weighs more than the stay.

sysselsatta_hotell_restaurang_andel.name: Employed in hotels and restaurants, share of all working in the municipality
sysselsatta_hotell_restaurang_andel.note: Share of people employed at workplaces in the municipality in November 2024, almost twice Dalarna (3.3%) and Sweden (3.75%). With 4,324 employed that is about 300 people (own calculation); the municipality calls tourism its largest private industry.

sysselsatta_vard_omsorg_andel.name: Employed in health and social care, share of all working in the municipality
sysselsatta_vard_omsorg_andel.note: Health care, elderly care and social services in November 2024; Dalarna 20.3%, Sweden 16.4%. The municipal and regional sector employs 34.5% of all who work in Rättvik (Sweden 23.3%), and the municipality is the largest employer with 1,056 permanent staff in 2025.

sysselsatta_bygg_andel.name: Employed in construction, share of all working in the municipality
sysselsatta_bygg_andel.note: November 2024; Dalarna 8.9%, Sweden 7.1%. The share has been 11–11.5% since 2020.

sysselsatta_tillverkning_andel.name: Employed in manufacturing and mining, share of all working in the municipality
sysselsatta_tillverkning_andel.note: November 2024; Dalarna 14.3%, Sweden 10.7%. The municipality counts the wood industry among its main industries; the share has fallen from 10.6% in 2020.

sysselsatta_jord_skog_andel.name: Employed in agriculture, forestry and fishing, share of all working in the municipality
sysselsatta_jord_skog_andel.note: November 2024; Dalarna 3.1%, Sweden 1.8%. The share was 6.3% in 2020.

storsta_privata_arbetsgivare.name: Largest private employer (Rättvik Event AB, which runs Dalhalla), employees
storsta_privata_arbetsgivare.note: SCB size class 250–299 employees in November 2025, shown as 275 by Ekonomifakta; the figure reflects many seasonal and hourly staff. That the largest private employer is an events company shows the weight of tourism; the municipality itself had 1,056 permanent staff.

gastnatter_per_ankomst.name: Average length of stay (guest nights per arrival)
gastnatter_per_ankomst.note: 20.66 guest nights per inhabitant divided by 9.02 arrivals per inhabitant = 2.29 nights per arrival, equivalent to about 99,100 arrivals in 2025 (9.024 × 10,978). In 2019 the stay was 2.64 nights; Dalarna 3.12, Sweden 2.00, Leksand 1.89, Mora 1.95 and Orsa 2.54 (2025).

besparing_socialforvaltning.name: Savings requirement in elderly care and disability services (social services)
besparing_socialforvaltning.note: The social services department needed to cut costs by about SEK 25 million and gave notice on about 60 posts in elderly care and disability services in February 2025. It still overran its budget by SEK 5.6 million in 2025, and without the Dala Energi capital gain the municipality's result was SEK 14.8 million (1.7% of taxes and grants, below the 2% target).

foretagsklimat_ranking.name: Business climate, rank among 290 municipalities (Svenskt Näringsliv)
foretagsklimat_ranking.note: Rank 65 in the 2026 ranking (72 in 2025, 50 in 2024, best 31 in 2018 and worst 240 in 2009); firms' overall rating is 4.0 out of 6 against the Swedish average 3.5. In Dalarna, Orsa ranks 53, Leksand 76 and Mora 153.

brp_per_invanare.name: Gross regional product (GRP) per inhabitant
brp_per_invanare.note: The municipality's GRP was SEK 3,751 million in 2024 at current prices, 56% of the national average per inhabitant (SEK 606 thousand); Leksand 424, Mora 492 and Orsa 282. Per employed person SEK 834 thousand against Sweden's 1,184, reflecting labour-intensive industries such as tourism, retail and care and a large share of older residents.

foretagare_andel_sysselsatta.name: Business owners as a share of the employed
foretagare_andel_sysselsatta.note: 833 business owners in 2024 (844 the year before), rank 29 of 290; Dalarna 10.6%, Sweden 9.9%. Small firms with fewer than 50 employees have 2,008 jobs, 46% of all jobs in the municipality (p. 11).

aldrande_befolkning.title: An ageing population
aldrande_befolkning.text: The dependency ratio is 1.09, among the highest in Sweden (country 0.77), and the number of 85–89-year-olds is expected to rise by 74% by 2034. Deaths are twice the births, so Rättvik needs about a hundred more people moving in than out each year not to shrink; in 2022–2025 it was between 16 and 67.

kompetens.title: Who will work in the schools and in care?
kompetens.text: The average age of the municipality's 1,056 permanent staff is 47, and many teachers, preschool teachers and assistant nurses will retire. Meanwhile 63% of young people think they will move away.

skolresultat.title: School results and the village schools
skolresultat.text: The share of year-9 pupils passing all subjects fell to 66.3%, while upper-secondary graduation within three years rose to 88%. There are fewer children and preschool groups are closing – and the village schools are part of the Rättvik model.

va_natet.title: Old water and sewer pipes
va_natet.text: About 600 km of pipes, most built in 1955–1979, are to be renewed with borrowed money. Charges rose 20% in 2025 and 5% in 2026, and the group's debt is 113,000 kronor per inhabitant, mostly for water and sewerage.

skyfall_hogvatten.title: Cloudbursts and Lake Siljan's high water
skyfall_hogvatten.text: Storm Hans in August 2023 damaged some 150 houses in the municipality and destroyed 25 km of road. Siljan's 100-year level already reaches the beach and almost half the campsite, and the high water is expected to rise a little in a warmer climate with wetter winters.

vard_i_byarna.title: Care close by – in the villages too
vard_i_byarna.text: Region Dalarna's healthcare bus to Furudal, Bingsjö and Boda, decided in 2023, has still not come. Agency doctors do 18% of the GP work at the county's health centres, and each GP has 1,775 listed patients on average.

ekonomi.title: A balanced budget
ekonomi.text: Without the one-off gain from the Dala Energi shares, the 2025 result was only 1.7%, below the 2% goal, and social services went over budget. The municipality's own investments are small: 42 million kronor in 2026.

fabodarna.title: The summer farms and the open landscape
fabodarna.text: Rättvik has 608 hectares of summer-farm pasture, two thirds of its pasture, and the summer-farm tradition has been on UNESCO's intangible heritage list since 2024. 437 dairy cows on five farms still cover all local milk.

besoksnaringen.title: Tourism
besoksnaringen.text: Tourism is the municipality's largest private industry: Lake Siljan, Långbryggan, Dalhalla, Classic Car Week and Vidablick. On the Saturday of Classic Car Week three times as many people are in Rättvik as usual.

naturbruket.title: Natural resource studies at Stiernhööksgymnasiet
naturbruket.text: The upper-secondary school's natural resource programme has its own school farm and a newly bought dairy, and 42 applied for 24 places as their first choice. School meals get meat, potatoes and grain from the farm.

foreningslivet.title: Associations and folk music
foreningslivet.text: 93 associations, 24 of them village-hall associations, and almost twice as many sports clubs per inhabitant as the country. “When three Rättvik people meet, four fiddles play.”

egen_energi.title: Own electricity and renewable heat
egen_energi.text: The municipality produced 105 GWh of electricity in 2024, three quarters of its use, mostly from wind, and district heating is 99% renewable. The municipality co-owns the grid and the district heating.

tillit.title: Safety and trust
tillit.text: Only 11% feel unsafe out in the evening and 73% trust other people, and child poverty is 9.4% against 12.9% in Sweden. Fewer are lonely than in Dalarna and the country.

siljan.title: Lake Siljan
siljan.text: Clear water with no algal blooms in 26 bathing-water samples in 2023–2026. The ice now stays about 74 days a year, against 129 days in the 1800s.

kommun_vision.title: Vision 2030 – Rättvik, where tradition meets the future
kommun_vision.text: Rättvik is to be a growing municipality that takes responsibility for future generations – ecologically, socially and economically sustainable, with attractive places to live across the municipality, small-scale business and a safe, inclusive society. The municipality calls its approach the Rättvik model: integration, keeping the villages and village schools, renewable energy, locally produced food and an open landscape. Its Agenda 2030 work began in 2016, when UNDP visited Rättvik as the first municipality in Sweden, and today has 94 local ambitions.
